definition_zh: 未被污染的；未受（有害物）沾染的；未受影响的；纯净的
definition_en: not polluted or spoiled, and not affected by anything harmful or unwanted
core_image: 一滴清水落进干净的杯子，杯壁一圈光洁，没有任何污迹
scene: 实验室里，研究员用干净的手套取出一份水样，确认它没有受到任何污染。Back in the lab, the researcher checked that the sample of water was uncontaminated.
sceneCN: 这里 uncontaminated 是「未被污染的」（第 1 个义项：环境被污物或毒物侵害、变脏）。句意：回到实验室后，研究员确认这份水样未被污染。

pos.zh: 未被污染的；未受有害物沾染的；未受影响的；纯净的

derivatives.zh: contaminate 来自拉丁语 contaminare（接触而弄脏）；此词加 un- 与 -ed 表示「没有被弄脏」
contaminate 加 -ation（动作或结果），义为「污染；沾染」
contaminate 加 -ant（造成某事的事物），义为「污染物」
前缀 de-（去除）加 contaminate，义为「清除污染」
un- 加 contaminable，义为「无法被污染的」

senses.title: Not polluted by dirt or poison
senses.definition: free from harmful substances such as germs, chemicals, or waste
senses.definitionCN: 不含细菌、化学物质或废弃物等有害成分
senses.example: Villagers walked miles to fill their bottles with uncontaminated water.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们走很远的路去打未被污染的水。
senses.why: The Latin verb contaminare comes from a root meaning to touch, so pollution is contact with a defiling thing; un- plus the past participle says that contact never happened.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 contaminare 源于表「接触、触碰」的词根，所以污染就是碰上了脏东西；un- 加上过去分词表示那种接触从来没有发生。

senses.title: Not mixed with unwanted material
senses.titleCN: 未被掺杂的；没有混入杂质的
senses.definition: holding only what it should hold, without added or stray material
senses.definitionCN: 只包含本该包含的成分，没有混入的东西
senses.example: The flour in the tin was uncontaminated by sawdust.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子里的面粉没有被木屑掺杂。
senses.why: Mixing is a kind of touching: a scoop that met sawdust leaves its trace, and the clean flour beside it is described by the same prefix of denial.
senses.whyCN: 混杂也是一种接触：舀过木屑的勺子会留下痕迹，旁边干净的面粉就用同一个否定前缀来修饰。

senses.title: Not spoiled by anything else
senses.titleCN: （资料、证据等）未受干扰的；未毁损的
senses.definition: kept whole and unaltered, said of evidence, records, or food
senses.definitionCN: 保持完整、未被改动，多指证据、记录或食物
senses.example: The sample had to stay uncontaminated until the last test.
senses.exampleCN: 样本必须保持未受干扰，直到最后一项检测。
senses.why: Once contamination names the spoiling of an experiment, the word follows any evidence that others could touch, spoil, or rework.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「污染」用来指实验被搅坏，这个词便跟着指任何可能被他人触碰、破坏或改动的证据。

senses.title: Not influenced by outside views
senses.titleCN: （判断、观点）未受影响的；纯粹的
senses.definition: said of an opinion or feeling that no outside pressure or prejudice has shaped
senses.definitionCN: 形容看法或感受没有受到外来压力或偏见的影响
senses.example: She kept a plain and uncontaminated view of right and wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 她对是非保持着朴素而未被外界污染的看法。
senses.why: A touch can be a pressure just out of view, so the same image turns abstract: a mind is contaminated by influence and uncontaminated without it.
senses.whyCN: 触碰也可以是看不见的施压，于是同一意象转向抽象：头脑会被人影响「污染」，不受影响便是 uncontaminated。

senses.title: In its original and pure state
senses.definition: in science and scholarship, describing something that has kept its earliest form without change
senses.definitionCN: 在科学与学术语境中，指保持最初形态、未经改变的事物
senses.example: Isolated valleys can keep an uncontaminated version of an old dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 偏僻的山谷可以保存一种未受外来影响的古老方言。
senses.why: Before a modern idea of pollution, scholars spoke of language and custom being spoiled by outside contact, and this sense survives in learned writing.
senses.whyCN: 在现代「污染」概念出现之前，学者就说语言与风俗会被外来接触弄得走样，这一义项留存于学术写作中。

senses.title: Free of bacteria and other life
senses.definition: kept free of living organisms, as a medical tool or a sealed container
senses.definitionCN: 没有微生物，指医疗器械或密封容器
senses.example: The jar of jam stayed uncontaminated for a full season.
senses.exampleCN: 那罐果酱一整季都没有受到细菌感染。
senses.why: In medicine the touching becomes literally biological: the hand that touches the wound brings the germ, and the tool that was never touched stays uncontaminated.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，这种「接触」变成字面上的生物过程：碰到伤口的手会带来细菌，而从未被触碰的器械就保持清洁。

intro.en: Uncontaminated is the negative adjective of the Latin verb contaminare, with un- in front and -ed behind, next to the older English noun taint.
intro.cn: uncontaminated 是拉丁语动词 contaminare 的否定形容词形式，前面加 un-、后面加 -ed；它与更早的英语名词 taint 同族。

items.en: The verb contaminare means to defile by contact, and the noun contamen names that defilement.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 contaminare 意为「因接触而弄脏」，名词 contamen 指这种污染。

items.en: The root is usually reconstructed as tag-, to touch, which also underlies Latin tangere.
items.cn: 词根一般认为可重构为 tag-，意为「接触」，拉丁语 tangere 也出于此。

items.en: From the same root comes tinctus, a dipping or a stain, through tingere, to dip.
items.cn: 同一词根还给出 tinctus（浸染、污渍），经由 tingere（浸）。

items.en: Old French contemnare and the past participle carry the meaning into French as defilement.
items.cn: 古法语 contemnare 与其过去分词把这个含义带入法语，表示污损。

items.en: Contaminate enters English with the sense of defiling by contact, and forms such as uncontaminated follow.
items.cn: contaminate 约自十五世纪进入英语，意为「因接触而弄脏」，uncontaminated 这类形式随后出现。

note.en: Uncontaminated belongs to the contamination family, and its nearest neighbours in meaning are clean, pure, and uncontaminated adjectives such as unpolluted.
note.cn: uncontaminated 属于「污染」词族，意义上的近邻是 clean、pure 以及 unpolluted 这类形容词。

entries.definition: to make dirty or harmful
the state of being polluted
a substance that pollutes
free from dirt or unwanted matter
not mixed with anything else
not damaged by waste or harmful substances

normalIntro.en: Read uncontaminated as un-, contaminate, and -ed, and keep the image of a hand that never touches the dirt.
normalIntro.cn: 把 uncontaminated 读成 un-、contaminate 与 -ed 三部分，并记住「那只从未碰到脏东西的手」的画面。

normal.en: Un- denies, contaminate pollutes, and -ed marks a lasting state, so no pollution ever landed.
normal.cn: un- 表否定，contaminate 是「污染」，-ed 表示持续状态，合起来就是「污染从未落到上面」。

normal.en: The root con- plus taminar- suggests touching together, which is exactly how defilement spreads.
normal.cn: 词根 con- 加 taminar- 有「碰到一起」的意思，而玷污正是这样传播的。

normal.en: The related noun taint is short and familiar, so remember that taint and contaminate are cousins.
normal.cn: 相关的名词 taint 简短又好记，记住 taint 与 contaminate 是同族表亲。

normal.en: In news style, uncontaminated water is a fixed and reassuring phrase.
normal.cn: 在新闻写法里，uncontaminated water 是一个固定的、让人安心的说法。

normal.en: The prefix de- in decontaminate reverses the pollution, which shows the root from the other side.
normal.cn: decontaminate 里的前缀 de- 与污染相反，从另一面显示了这个词根。

abstract.en: See a drop of clean water in an empty glass, with nothing swimming in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空杯里的一滴清水，水里没有任何东西在游动。

abstract.en: Imagine a white lab glove lifting a sample without ever brushing a dirty surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白色实验手套拿起样本，从未擦到任何脏的表面。

abstract.en: Picture an old jar of flour opened after years, still white and sweet.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐存放多年的旧面粉被打开，依然白净、没有任何异味。

examples.en: The children were told to drink only uncontaminated water.
examples.cn: 孩子们被告知只能喝未受污染的水。

examples.en: The museum keeps the coins uncontaminated by industrial air.
examples.cn: 博物馆让这些钱币免受工业空气的污染。

examples.en: An uncontaminated sample is essential for a fair test.
examples.cn: 一次公正的测试必须依赖未受污染的样本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安它米内」——把干净的水安安全全地留在米袋内部，谁也没碰过它，所以没被污染；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为词根可重构为 tag-（接触），拉丁语 tingere（浸染）与 tangere（触碰）同出此源；拉丁语 contaminare（接触而弄脏）→ 英语 contaminate（污染）；加否定前缀 un- 与过去分词 -ed 构成 uncontaminated，核心义「没有被碰脏」。

sensesIntro.en: Uncontaminated runs from physical dirt and poison to mixed materials, spoiled evidence, unswayed opinion, unaltered tradition, and finally microscopic life.
sensesIntro.cn: uncontaminated 从有形的脏物与毒物出发，扩展到掺杂、被破坏的证据、不受影响的看法、未被改动的传统，最后落到肉眼看不见的微生物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of clean water meeting nothing but the walls of a clean glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴清水除了干净杯壁什么都没有碰到。

branches.en: Water and flour show the plain physical sense of no pollution and no mixing.
branches.cn: 水与面粉体现「无污染、无掺杂」最朴素的物理义项。

branches.en: Evidence is treated like water: it must not be spoiled by contact.
branches.cn: 证据被当作水来对待：不能因接触而被破坏。

branches.en: The touch turns invisible when it is influence on a mind.
branches.cn: 当「触碰」落在思想上，它就变成看不见的影响。

branches.en: A language keeps its oldest form when outside contact is denied.
branches.cn: 一种语言在没有外来接触时才能保留最古老的形态。

branches.en: The medical and the everyday senses both rest on germ-free cleanliness.
branches.cn: 医学义与日常义都落在「没有细菌的洁净」之上。

intro.en: Uncontaminated joins the English prefix un- and the participle suffix -ed to the Latin verb contaminare and its relatives.
intro.cn: uncontaminated 把英语前缀 un- 与分词后缀 -ed 接在拉丁语动词 contaminare 及其亲属词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin contaminare, to defile by contact, gives contaminate, and its relatives contamen and contumelia, a wrong done by touch, stand beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 contaminare（接触而弄脏）给出 contaminate；同族的 contamen 与 contumelia（因接触而施加的侮辱）在旁呼应。

items.example: Un- marks the absence of pollution.
items.exampleCN: un- 表示没有污染。

items.example: Contaminare is the direct source of contaminate.
items.exampleCN: contaminare 是 contaminate 的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix con- marks contact.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 表示接触。

items.example: The tamin root links contaminate with taint.
items.exampleCN: tamin 词根把 contaminate 与 taint 连在一起。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms the verb contaminate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成动词 contaminate。

items.example: The suffix -ed marks the resulting state.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 标记结果状态。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms contamination.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 contamination。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms contaminant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ant 构成 contaminant。

items.example: The prefix de- makes decontaminate remove the pollution.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 使 decontaminate 表示清除污染。

definition_zh: 非传统的；非常规的；不落俗套的；不合惯例的
definition_en: not following the usual or accepted way of doing things, and often surprising or original
core_image: 一屋子人整齐地沿直线走，只有一个人拐了个弯另辟小路
scene: 设计课上，大家按部就班地画方桌，只有同学画了一张扭曲的椅子并说这样更舒服。In the design class, a student sketched an unconventional chair that curved like a wave.
sceneCN: 这里 unconventional 是「非常规的、不落俗套的」（第 1 个义项：不符合人们习惯的做法或样式）。句意：在设计课上，一名学生画了一把像波浪一样弯曲的非常规椅子。

pos.zh: 非传统的；非常规的；不落俗套的

derivatives.zh: 来自拉丁语 convenire（聚集、一致），义为「惯例；大会」；此词加否定前缀后表示「不循惯例」
convention 加 -al（与……有关的），义为「常规的；传统的」
unconventional 加 -ly，义为「非常规地」
unconventional 加 -ity（性质），义为「非常规性」
与 convention 同源，来自拉丁语 convenire，义为「召集；开会」

senses.title: Not following accepted custom
senses.definition: done or made in a way that most people do not expect or usually approve of
senses.definitionCN: 做法或样式与大多数人的预期或习惯不符
senses.example: The team tried an unconventional route to the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 这个队伍尝试了一条非常规的登顶路线。
senses.why: The Latin verb convenire means to come together, and a convention is where people agree on one way; un- denies the agreement, so the person simply does not come along.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 convenire 意为「聚到一起」，convention 就是大家商定的同一种做法；un- 否定了这种商定，也就是这个人干脆没有跟着走。

senses.title: Rather strange and surprising
senses.definition: not usual in a way that surprises or puzzles other people
senses.definitionCN: 与寻常不同，令人惊讶或困惑
senses.example: Her answers were unconventional enough to shock the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答不合常规到让评审团大为震惊。
senses.why: Whatever leaves the shared road looks odd from the road itself, so the same denial of custom becomes a mild word for strange.
senses.whyCN: 任何离开共同道路的东西，从路上看都显得古怪；于是同一个否定「惯例」的前缀也成了「奇怪」的婉转说法。

senses.title: Clearly original and inventive
senses.definition: fresh and imaginative because it refuses the obvious pattern
senses.definitionCN: 因为拒绝显而易见的套式而显得新鲜、有想象力
senses.example: The chef is known for unconventional pairings of sweet and sour.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主厨以甜酸搭配的非常规组合著称。
senses.why: Once the word stopped being a criticism, it turned into praise: the one who breaks the shared habit is the one who invents something new.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词不再是批评，它就成了赞赏：打破共同习惯的人，正是发明新东西的人。

senses.title: Not designed like ordinary versions
senses.titleCN: （建筑、技术）非标准的；非常规的
senses.definition: describing a design, method, or structure that deliberately avoids the standard model
senses.definitionCN: 形容设计、方法或结构有意避开标准样式
senses.example: The house is an unconventional shape with no straight walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这座房子形状非常规，没有一面直墙。
senses.why: Building standards are written agreements too, so a structure that ignores the standard plan takes the same prefix of refusal.
senses.whyCN: 建筑标准同样是一种写下来的约定，所以无视标准图的建筑也用同一个表示拒绝的前缀。

senses.title: Not approved by the experts
senses.titleCN: （做法、手段）未经公认的；非正统的
senses.definition: used of medical or technical methods outside the accepted professional practice
senses.definitionCN: 指医学或技术方法超出一致的专业做法
senses.example: She managed the pain with unconventional treatments.
senses.exampleCN: 她用非常规的办法缓解疼痛。
senses.why: A convention can be a professional agreement, and a practice outside the agreed method is literally without that agreement.
senses.whyCN: 惯例也可以是专业人士的共识，而落在共识方法之外的做法，字面上就「没有那个共识」。

senses.title: Having a free private life
senses.titleCN: （生活方式）不循常规的；不拘一格的
senses.definition: said of a lifestyle or personal style that ignores social rules of dress and family
senses.definitionCN: 形容生活方式或个人风格不理会衣着与家庭方面的社会规矩
senses.example: His unconventional household puzzled the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他那种不循常规的家庭生活让邻居们摸不着头脑。
senses.why: Social custom is the deepest set of shared habits, so a life lived outside them is the plainest form of this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 社会习俗是最深层的一整套共同习惯，所以在它之外过的一生，就是这个形容词最直接的形式。

senses.title: In the manner of an outsider
senses.definition: describing work or people that belong to the margins rather than the mainstream
senses.definitionCN: 形容作品或人不属于主流而处于边缘
senses.example: The gallery shows unconventional artists from small towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出小城镇的另类艺术家。
senses.why: The road most people take is the mainstream, and whoever walks beside it is described by the same denial of the common way.
senses.whyCN: 大多数人走的那条路就是主流，走在它旁边的人，就用同一个否定「共同之路」的词来描写。

intro.en: Unconventional is the English prefix un- laid on conventional, which goes back through French to the Latin verb convenire, to come together and agree.
intro.cn: unconventional 是英语前缀 un- 加在 conventional 之上；conventional 经法语上溯到拉丁语动词 convenire，意为「聚到一起、达成一致」。

items.en: The verb convenire joins com-, together, to venire, to come; it means to assemble or to agree.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 convenire 由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）合成，意为聚集或达成一致。

items.en: The noun conventio names a coming together, an agreement, or a pact.
items.cn: 名词 conventio 指聚到一起、一致或协定。

items.en: The form convention reaches French with the sense of an agreement and a shared custom.
items.cn: convention 这一形式进入法语，含义为协定与共同习俗。

items.en: Convention enters English around 1400, first as an agreement and later as an agreed custom.
items.cn: convention 约于十五世纪初进入英语，先是「协定」，后指「公认的习俗」。

items.en: Conventional appears as an adjective and is soon given the negative prefix, so that unconventional can praise as well as criticise.
items.cn: conventional 作为形容词出现后很快被加上否定前缀，于是 unconventional 既能批评，也能赞赏。

note.en: Unconventional shares its root with convention and convene, and in meaning it sits between unusual and unorthodox.
note.cn: unconventional 与 convention、convene 同根，在意义上介于 unusual 与 unorthodox 之间。

entries.definition: a usual way or an agreed custom
following the usual custom
to come together for a meeting
not following the accepted belief or method
not happening or seen often
behaving in ways others find odd

normalIntro.en: Unconventional is read as un-, convention, and -al, and the convention is simply the road everyone agreed to walk.
normalIntro.cn: 把 unconventional 读成 un-、convention 与 -al，而 convention 不过是大家一致同意要走的那条路。

normal.en: Un- denies, convention names the accepted custom, and -al makes the adjective, so the word means off the agreed road.
normal.cn: un- 表否定，convention 指公认的习俗，-al 构成形容词，所以这个词就是「不在约定的路上」。

normal.en: In Latin, com- plus venire gives convenire, to come together, which is why convene and convention look alike.
normal.cn: 在拉丁语里 com- 加 venire 得到 convenire（走到一起），这就是 convene 与 convention 长得相似的原因。

normal.en: The contrast is built in: put conventional and unconventional side by side and watch one letter change everything.
normal.cn: 对比是现成的：把 conventional 与 unconventional 并排放，看一个字母如何改变一切。

normal.en: A common phrase is an unconventional approach, which often says brave rather than wrong.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 an unconventional approach，它常常表示「勇敢」，而不是「错误」。

normal.en: The same root hides in investigate and invent, so the ven- family keeps the idea of coming to something.
normal.cn: 同一个词根也藏在 investigate 与 invent 里，ven- 这一族都保留了「走向某处」的意思。

abstract.en: See a crowd walking in one straight line and one person turning quietly down a side path.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人沿一条直线走，只有一个人悄悄拐进旁边的小路。

abstract.en: Picture a chair whose legs bend like waves while every other chair stands square.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅腿像波浪般弯曲的椅子，而其他椅子都方正得像方砖。

abstract.en: Imagine a door painted on the roof, because that is where someone decided a door belongs.
abstract.cn: 想象在屋顶上画一扇门，因为有人认定门就该开在那儿。

examples.en: Their unconventional plan worked better than the usual one.
examples.cn: 他们那种非常规的计划比常规计划更有效。

examples.en: He is unconventional in the way he dresses at work.
examples.cn: 他在上班时的穿着方式不循常规。

examples.en: The coach won the match with an unconventional set of tactics.
examples.cn: 教练用一套非常规的战术赢下了比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安混文迅恼」——大家安静地把文章写在一处、快速记住，唯独他一个人嫌闷恼，偏要换条路走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起）+ venire（来）→ convenire（聚集、达成一致）→ conventio（协定）→ 古法语 convention → 英语 convention（惯例）→ conventional（常规的）；加否定前缀 un- 构成 unconventional，核心义「不在大家约定的那条路上」。

sensesIntro.en: Unconventional begins with a plain refusal of custom, shades into surprise, turns into praise for originality, and then spreads to design, medicine, private life, and the margins.
sensesIntro.cn: unconventional 从朴素的「不循习俗」出发，滑向「奇怪」，变成对独创的赞美，再扩展到设计、医学、私人生活与边缘地带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker who steps off the agreed road onto a side path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个走开约定大路、拐上旁路的人。

branches.en: The plain refusal of the agreed way is the base sense.
branches.cn: 对约定之路的朴素拒绝是基本义。

branches.en: Once off the road, the walker looks strange to the crowd on it.
branches.cn: 一旦离开大路，这个人在路上的人看来就显得古怪。

branches.en: Stepping aside becomes inventiveness when the side path leads somewhere better.
branches.cn: 当旁路通向更好的地方，离群就变成了创造力。

branches.en: Designs and treatments also have standard plans to refuse.
branches.cn: 设计与治疗同样有可拒绝的标准方案。

branches.en: Private life is where the shared habit bites hardest, so the word fits a free household.
branches.cn: 私人生活是共同习惯约束最紧之处，所以这个词适合形容自由的家庭生活。

intro.en: Unconventional is built on the Latin root ven-, to come, with the prefix com- and the English affixes un-, -ion, and -al.
intro.cn: unconventional 建立在拉丁词根 ven-（来）之上，配有前缀 com- 与英语词缀 un-、-ion 与 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin convenire, to come together, gives convene and convention, and its verb venire, to come, sits at the bottom of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 convenire（走到一起）给出 convene 与 convention，其底层的动词 venire 意为「来」。

items.example: Un- denies the convention.
items.exampleCN: un- 否定惯例。

items.example: The prefix con- brings people together.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 表示人们聚在一起。

items.example: The ven root also sits inside invent and prevent.
items.exampleCN: ven 词根也出现在 invent 与 prevent 中。

items.example: Venire is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: venire 是整族词的底层。

items.example: Convenire is where convention begins.
items.exampleCN: convention 从 convenire 开始。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms the noun convention.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成名词 convention。

items.example: The suffix -al forms conventional.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 conventional。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unconventionally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 unconventionally。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms unconventionality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 unconventionality。

definition_zh: 估量不足；看轻；把……想得比实际小
definition_en: to think that something is smaller, cheaper, weaker, or less important than it really is, or to guess a value that turns out to be too low
core_image: 一只脚踩在量尺的一端，把要量的东西压得比实际矮了一截
scene: 预算会上，工程师说这栋老楼翻新最多花三个月，结果光拆旧墙就用掉了半年。The project manager clearly underestimated how many permits the renovation needed.
sceneCN: 这里 underestimate 是「低估、估量不足」（第 1 个义项：把事物的数量或难度想得比实际小）；句意为项目经理显然低估了翻新工程需要多少个许可。

pos.zh: 估量不足；看轻；把……估计过低
估低的判断；偏低的估计值

derivatives.zh: 加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「估量不足；偏低判断」
过去分词作形容词，义为「被看轻的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「加以看轻的、容易把量估少的」

senses.title: To judge a number or amount as too small
senses.definition: to think that a number, amount, or figure is smaller than it really is, so that your own guess comes out too low
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个数量或数字比实际情况小，结果自己给出的估计偏低
senses.example: Researchers underestimated the number of visitors by about half.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员把游客数量估低了大约一半。
senses.why: The Latin stem from which estimate comes means to value or determine the worth of something, so under- simply adds the idea that the valued figure has been placed below the true one.
senses.whyCN: estimate 所源的拉丁词干意为「估量、评定价值」，加上表示「在下」的 under-，就是把估出来的数目放在真实值之下，于是「低估数量」直接从这个刻度的画面长出来。

senses.title: To fail to see the strength or difficulty of something
senses.titleCN: 看轻难度；轻视对手或危险
senses.definition: to treat a difficulty, an opponent, or a risk as weaker or easier than it really is
senses.definitionCN: 把困难、对手或风险看得比实际更弱、更容易
senses.example: Never underestimate the power of a short, vivid example.
senses.exampleCN: 永远不要低估一个简短生动例子的力量。
senses.why: Under the amount lies the strength: when the hidden quantity is force or difficulty rather than a figure, calling it smaller means treating it as easy to beat or easy to finish.
senses.whyCN: 数量之下其实是力量：当被藏起来的量是实力或难度而不是数字时，把它说小就等于当成好对付、好完成，于是同一画面顺势变成「轻视」。

senses.title: To predict something smaller, cheaper, or shorter than it turns out to be
senses.titleCN: 把成本、时间或作用看轻
senses.definition: to say that a cost, a period of time, or an effect will be less than it turns out to be
senses.definitionCN: 宣称某项成本、一段时间或某种作用会比后来实际发生的更小
senses.example: The planners underestimated the travel time from the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者把从机场出发的路程时间估少了。
senses.why: Here the low figure is attached to cost, time, or impact, and the word describes the outcome of the whole estimate rather than a single number in a report.
senses.whyCN: 这时被压低的是成本、时间或影响力，词描述的是整个估测的结果，而不只是报告里的某一个数字。

senses.title: The noun for a low estimate
senses.definition: a guess or judgement that turns out to be too low, or an estimate given very low
senses.definitionCN: 事后证明偏低的一估，或一个给得很低的估计
senses.example: That figure is a serious underestimate of the true cost.
senses.exampleCN: 那个数字把真实成本估得太低了。
senses.why: English freely uses one form as both verb and noun, so the very act just described turns straight into its own name, as in gross underestimate.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯让同一个词形兼作动词和名词，于是刚描述的那个动作直接变成它自己的名字，形成「严重偏低的一估」这样的说法。

intro.en: Underestimate is an English compound of the native Old English under and the Latin-derived verb estimate, which entered English through French from a Latin stem for valuing.
intro.cn: underestimate 是英语自造的复合词，由本土古英语 under 与源自拉丁、经法语进入英语的 estimate 组成，后面的词干意为「估量、评定价值」。

items.en: Under is a native preposition meaning beneath or below, and it is the source of the first half of the word.
items.cn: under 是本土介词，意为「在……之下」，也是这个词前半部分的来源。

items.en: The Latin verb aestimare means to value or appraise; its own origin is uncertain, but it is generally taken as the remote source of estimate.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 aestimare 意为「估量、评定价值」，其自身来源不确定，但一般认为是 estimate 的远源。

items.en: French carried the stem east and west as estimer, and English met it in medieval borrowing.
items.cn: 法语以 estimer 的形式传承这个词干，英语在中古时期的借用中接触到它。

items.en: English forms the verb estimate, meaning to judge the value or size of something.
items.cn: 英语构成动词 estimate，意为评判某物的价值或大小。

items.en: Under and estimate combine into underestimate; the Oxford English Dictionary records the verb in the seventeenth century, and the noun use comes later.
items.cn: under 与 estimate 组合成 underestimate；《牛津英语词典》记录的动词用法始于十七世纪，名词用法更晚。

items.en: From prices and sizes the verb expands to strength, danger, and human ability, where it often carries a warning tone.
items.cn: 从价格与数量扩展到实力、危险与人的能力，此时常带提醒意味。

note.en: The first group shows the estimate family; the second shows its usual opposites and its close neighbours for judging size or strength.
note.cn: 第一组是 estimate 词族；第二组是它的常见反义词以及判断大小、强弱的近邻。

entries.definition: to judge the size, value, or cost of something roughly
entries.definitionCN: 粗略判断某物的大小、价值或花费，同根基础词

entries.definition: the act or result of valuing something too low
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ion 构成的名词，义为「估低、估量不足」

entries.definition: the past participle used of a person or figure judged too low
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，义为「被看轻的；被估少的」

entries.definition: to judge that something is bigger or more important than it is
entries.definitionCN: 高估；把某物看得比实际更大或更重要

entries.definition: to place too low a value or worth on something
entries.definitionCN: 把……的价值看得过低；认为……不值

entries.definition: to rate or judge something as less good than it is
entries.definitionCN: 把……的评分看得过低；看轻

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the under- prefix, the estimate family, and the everyday collocations; the abstract hooks turn the low reading on a scale into a picture.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 under- 前缀、estimate 词族和日常搭配；抽象记忆点把量尺上读低的刻度变成画面。

normal.en: Under- means below, so to underestimate is to give a figure that sits below the truth.
normal.cn: under- 表示在下面：就是把一个数字放到真实值下面去。

normal.en: Estimate is the neutral verb; underestimate and overestimate are the two ends of the scale.
normal.cn: estimate 是中性动作；两头的词分别压低和抬高估计值。

normal.en: Pair the word with never and it becomes a fixed warning opening in exams.
normal.cn: 配上 never 就成考试里常见的提醒句开头。

normal.en: A gross underestimate is far below the real figure.
normal.cn: a gross underestimate 就是比真实值低得离谱的那个数字。

normal.en: Compare underrate and undervalue: both judge worth low, while underestimate often targets numbers, time, or difficulty.
normal.cn: 对比 underrate 与 undervalue：都指把价值看低，而目标词更常针对数字、时间和难度。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the true weight sits at ten and the reading needle stops at four.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤，真实重量停在十，指针却只指向四。

abstract.en: Imagine pressing a soft mattress down before guessing how tall it is.
abstract.cn: 想象先把床垫按扁，再去猜它有多高。

abstract.en: Think of a small enemy flag that hides a whole army behind the hill.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡后藏着整支军队，却只露出一面小旗。

examples.en: The engineers underestimated the cost of the bridge by a wide margin.
examples.cn: 工程师们把这座桥的造价估少了很大一截。

examples.en: Do not underestimate how long it takes to master a second language.
examples.cn: 不要把掌握一门第二语言所需的时间估得太短。

examples.en: Analysts called the sales forecast a gross underestimate.
examples.cn: 分析师说这份销售预测比实际情况低得离谱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德斯提米特」——把米特（米尺）下面的一段偷偷藏起来，量出来自然矮一截；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 本土古英语 under（在下面）+ estimate（源自拉丁 aestimare「估量、评定价值」，经古法语进入英语）→ 英语复合词 underestimate「把估量结果放在真实值之下」；词根可靠；《牛津英语词典》记录的动词用法始于十七世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Underestimate always places a judgement lower than the truth: first a number, then strength or difficulty, then cost or time in the making, and finally the low estimate itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: underestimate 始终把判断放在真实之下：先是数字，再是实力与难度，再是正在形成的成本与时间，最后让这个偏低的估计自己变成名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot pressing down on one end of a measuring scale, so the thing being measured reads shorter than it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚踩在量尺的一端，被量的东西于是显得比实际矮了一截。

branches.en: NUMBER: a count or figure is judged smaller than the real one, so the guess comes out too low.
branches.cn: 数字：数量或数字被看得比真实的小，估计结果因此偏低。

branches.en: FORCE: the hidden quantity is strength, danger, or ability, and calling it small means treating it as easy to beat.
branches.cn: 力量：被藏起的量是实力、危险或能力，说它小就是当作容易对付。

branches.en: TIME AND COST: the low figure is attached to money, hours, or impact, and the word names the outcome of a whole estimate.
branches.cn: 时间与成本：被压低的是钱、工时或影响，词指的是整个估测的结果。

branches.en: Both fix a low reading on a scale, one for a count in a report and one for a cost that only shows up later.
branches.cn: 两者都是在刻度上读低：一个针对报告里的计数，一个针对后来才显现的成本。

branches.en: A person can be underestimated as a rival, and the whole judgement can then be named as an underestimate.
branches.cn: 一个人可能作为对手被人看轻，而整个判断随后就被叫作一次估低。

intro.en: Underestimate is built from the native prefix under- and the borrowed verb estimate, not from a single Latin root; English simply adds the prefix to a word it had already taken in.
intro.cn: underestimate 由本土前缀 under- 与借入的动词 estimate 合成，并非来自一个拉丁词根；英语只是把前缀加到一个早已引入的词上。

latinIntro.en: The second element goes back to Latin aestimare, to value; English keeps its family in estimate, estimation, overestimate, and underestimate itself.
latinIntro.cn: 第二个成分可追溯到拉丁语 aestimare（估量价值）；英语把它的词族保存在 estimate、estimation、overestimate 以及 underestimate 本身里。

items.example: The prefix under- turns estimate into a low estimate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 把 estimate 变成偏低的估计。

items.meaning: to judge the size or value of something
items.example: Estimate is the base word without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: estimate 是不带前缀的基础词。

items.meaning: to judge something as bigger than it is
items.example: Overestimate sits at the other end of the scale.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 处在这根刻度的另一端。

items.meaningCN: 正在把量估少的（动名词或分词）
items.example: Underestimating the workload led to delays.
items.exampleCN: 把工作量估少了，导致了延误。

items.meaningCN: 被看作偏低的（过去分词或形容词）
items.example: The size of the market was underestimated.
items.exampleCN: 市场的规模被估少了。

items.meaning: the third person or plural form
items.example: The report underestimates the demand.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告把需求估少了。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms estimation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 estimation。

items.meaning: a judgement of value or size
items.example: Estimation is the noun of estimate.
items.exampleCN: estimation 是 estimate 的名词。

items.meaning: the act of valuing something too low
items.example: Underestimation of risk is a common error.
items.exampleCN: 把风险估少是常见的错误。

items.meaning: judged as less good than it is
items.example: An underrated player can still decide a match.
items.exampleCN: 一个被看轻的球员仍然能决定比赛。

definition_zh: 构成……的基础；在……之下；是……的潜在原因
definition_en: to be the real cause or basic support of something, or to lie under or behind something else
core_image: 岩层埋在草地之下，看不见，却托着地面上的一切
scene: 一张写满批注的地图摊在桌上，学生沿着旧船道一路追问，终于找到了两岸繁荣的原因。A network of old shipping routes underlies the wealth of the two port towns.
sceneCN: 这里 underlie 是「是……的深层原因、构成基础」（第 1 个义项：看不见的底层因素支撑着可见的现象）；句意为一张古老的航运网络构成了两座港口城镇财富的根基。

pos.zh: 构成……的基础；作为……的深层原因
位于……之下；在……的下面

collocations.zh: 是某种行为的潜在原因

derivatives.zh: 现在分词转形容词，义为「潜在的；根本的；下面的」
过去式形式，也表示「铺在下面」，如给地毯铺衬垫
金融术语，义为「标的资产」，即在合约底下被依靠的那个资产

senses.title: To be the hidden cause or basis of something
senses.titleCN: 构成……的深层原因；是……的基础
senses.definition: to be the real reason for, or the basic support of, an idea, problem, or situation that shows on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 作为表象背后的真正原因，或某个想法、问题、局面的基本依据
senses.example: Economic worries underlie much of the recent unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 近来的动荡很大程度上源于经济层面的忧虑。
senses.why: The verb keeps the plain spatial meaning of lying under; when an idea or a problem is placed under another one, the lower layer becomes the support and the reason for the visible layer above.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留「躺在下面」的空间本义；当把想法或问题放到另一件事底下时，下面那一层就成了支撑，也成了上面可见那一层的原因。

senses.title: To have something beneath it
senses.definition: to have a particular layer, feature, or body beneath the surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表层之下有某一层、某种特征或某个物体
senses.example: Thick clay underlies the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的黏土层铺满整个山谷的下方。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of meaning: the word describes solid matter lying under unbroken ground, with no claim about cause at all.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层意思：专指坚实的物质躺在连绵土地之下，完全不涉及因果。

senses.title: To support a claim or argument as its foundation
senses.titleCN: 作为论点或理论的基础；支撑
senses.definition: to support a claim, theory, or practice and to be what it stands on
senses.definitionCN: 支撑某个主张、理论或做法，并且是它据以成立的东西
senses.example: Evidence from three studies underlies the conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 结论的证据来自三项研究。
senses.why: A building stands on its foundation and an argument stands on its evidence, so the verb moves from earth under a house to proof under a claim.
senses.whyCN: 房子立在基础上，论证立在证据上；动词于是从「房屋下的土」走到「主张下的依据」。

senses.title: To be beneath the surface of another feature
senses.definition: to lie behind a visible feature or symptom and be less easy to notice
senses.definitionCN: 位于可见特征或症状背后，并且更不容易被注意到
senses.example: A deeper anxiety underlies his joking manner.
senses.exampleCN: 他玩笑的语气背后藏着更深的焦虑。
senses.why: When the word is used with feelings and symptoms it points at what lies under the surface, so the same picture explains both a skin rash and a nervous joke.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词配上情绪或症状时，它指的就是表面之下的东西，同一幅画面既能解释皮疹，也能解释玩笑背后的紧张。

intro.en: Underlie joins a native Old English prefix to a verb borrowed from Old English licgan, which is related to German liegen; the modern -lie spelling hides the older sound.
intro.cn: underlie 把本土古英语前缀 under 与来自古英语 licgan、和德语 liegen 同源的动词组合起来；现代拼写里的 -lie 遮住了更早的读音。

items.en: Licgan means to lie down or to be in a lying position, and it shares an ancestor with German liegen.
items.cn: licgan 意为「躺下、平卧」，与德语 liegen 同源。

items.en: The noun and verb forms split apart, and the verb survives as lie, whose past forms are lay and lain.
items.cn: 名词与动词形式逐渐分开，动词传下来是 lie，过去式和过去分词分别是 lay 与 lain。

items.en: Under is an old preposition meaning below, and the combination underly describes something lying beneath another thing.
items.cn: under 是意为「在下面」的古老介词，组合形式描述一物躺在另一物下方。

items.en: The full spelling underlie appears in the seventeenth century, alongside the spatial senses used by geologists.
items.cn: 完整拼写 underlie 在十七世纪出现，同时被地质学者用于描述地层。

items.en: From geology the verb moves to causes and arguments, giving the participle underlying, which matches the underlying layer in its original sense.
items.cn: 从地质学出发，这个词转到原因与论证上，并产出分词 underlying，其现代词义与它原本指的下层完全对应。

items.en: Analytic and legal writing now favours the verb wherever a cause or principle stands beneath visible facts.
items.cn: 在分析或法律写作中，凡有一个原因或原理立在可见事实之下，人们就偏好用这个词。

note.en: The first group gathers the lie family with its easily confused forms; the second gathers verbs for being the basis or cause of something.
note.cn: 第一组是 lie 词族，包含容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示「作为基础或原因」的动词。

entries.definition: existing beneath the surface as a cause or basic feature
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词转形容词，义为「潜在的；根本的；下面的」

entries.definition: the past tense, or a pad laid under a carpet
entries.definitionCN: 过去式，另作名词指铺在地毯下的衬垫

entries.definition: the past participle, as in the rock underlain by clay
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，用于被动结构，如「以黏土为底层的岩石」

entries.definition: to pass or wear away beneath, also used of cables and aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 从下方穿过或磨损，也用于缆线与飞机；与本词同构的前缀复合词

entries.definition: to support an argument or system from below
entries.definitionCN: 支撑；为……提供基础（常指论证或体系）

entries.definition: to hold something up or back it from below
entries.definitionCN: 支撑；托住，比本词更中性、更通用

entries.definition: to make something happen
entries.definitionCN: 引起；导致，只讲因果不讲层次

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the under- prefix, the lie family with its irregular past, and the underlying collocations; the abstract hooks see rock beneath a field.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 under- 前缀、lie 词族的不规则过去式和 underlying 搭配；抽象记忆点想象草原之下的岩层。

normal.en: Under- means below, and lie means to rest, so the layers rest out of sight.
normal.cn: under- 表示在下面，lie 表示躺着：那些层次就躺在看不见的地方。

normal.en: The forms run underlie, underlay, underlain, with an extra i in underlies.
normal.cn: 形式依次是 underlie、underlay、underlain，三单形式里多一个 i。

normal.en: An underlying cause sits behind the visible symptom.
normal.cn: underlying cause 就是藏在可见症状背后的那个原因。

normal.en: Compare underlie and underline: one lies under, one draws a line under.
normal.cn: 对比 underlie 与 underline：一个是躺在下面，一个是画线在下面。

normal.en: In geology the verb keeps its first sense, as when clay lies under rock.
normal.cn: 在地质语境里，这个词保留最早的意思，例如黏土躺在岩石之下。

abstract.en: Picture a field of grass on top of solid layers of rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一片青草盖在坚实的岩层之上。

abstract.en: Think of an iceberg whose weight sits under a thin white tip.
abstract.cn: 想象一座冰山，重量沉在薄薄的白色尖顶下面。

abstract.en: See a doctor reading a chart of layers beneath a patient skin, not the surface issue.
abstract.cn: 想象医生看的是一张皮肤之下的层次图，而不是表面那一点毛病。

examples.en: Poverty underlies many of the health problems reported in the district.
examples.cn: 这个地区报告的许多健康问题，根源都在贫困。

examples.en: A layer of sandstone underlies the thin soil.
examples.cn: 薄薄的土壤下面躺着一层砂岩。

examples.en: Researchers are still trying to find the mechanisms that underlie the disease.
examples.cn: 研究人员仍在寻找这种疾病背后的机制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德来的」——安德（under）的那一「赖」（来）着不动，就躺在下面当基础；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 本土古英语 under（在下面）+ lie（古英语 licgan「躺」，与德语 liegen 同源）→ 由 under 与 lie 组合成的复合动词，字面即「躺在……下面」，再引申为「构成底层、作为原因」；英语里 lie 与 lay 的历史纠缠使过去式写作 underlay。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts from a physical layer lying under another, then becomes the cause behind a visible effect, the evidence under a claim, and the feeling under a symptom.
sensesIntro.cn: underlie 从「物质层睡在另一层之下」出发，先变成可见结果背后的原因，再变成论点下的证据，最后变成症状背后的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rock bed asleep beneath a field, unseen and yet holding everything above in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片草地下沉睡着岩床，看不见，却托住了上面的一切。

branches.en: CAUSE: the lower layer becomes the reason for an unrest, worry, or problem above it.
branches.cn: 原因：下面那一层变成上方动荡、忧虑或问题的由来。

branches.en: SPACE: clay and sandstone lie under a valley, with no claim of cause at all.
branches.cn: 空间：黏土与砂岩躺在山谷之下，完全不涉及因果。

branches.en: SUPPORT: evidence and theory stand on the lower layer the way a house stands on its base.
branches.cn: 支撑：证据和理论立在下层之上，像房子立在底座上。

branches.en: Both work below the surface, one giving the reason and one hinting at what a person would rather hide.
branches.cn: 两者都发生在表面之下：一个提供原因，一个暗示患者不愿示人的东西。

branches.en: The plainest support is a geological bed, and the most abstract is a claim held up by its evidence.
branches.cn: 最实在的支撑是地质层，最抽象的支撑是由证据托住的主张。

intro.en: Underlie is a native English prefix on a native verb, so its parts are not bound Latin pieces; the common family member in modern texts is the participle underlying.
intro.cn: underlie 是本土前缀加本土动词，各成分并不是拉丁语的粘着部件；现代文本里最常用的家族成员是分词 underlying。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies at the heart of this verb; the related Latin verb for lying down, iacere, is listed here only for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词的核心没有拉丁来源；这里只列出意为「躺下」的拉丁语动词 iacere 作对照。

items.example: The prefix under- marks the lower position.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 标出较低的位置。

items.meaning: to rest flat in a position
items.example: The paper lies on the table.
items.exampleCN: 那张纸躺在桌上。

items.meaning: to rest beneath, or to be the cause below
items.meaningCN: 躺在下面；构成底层原因
items.example: Layers of clay underlie the garden.
items.exampleCN: 花园下面有好几层黏土。

items.meaningCN: 三单形式（原形中的 ie 变成 y）
items.example: That belief underlies the policy.
items.exampleCN: 那个信念是这项政策的依据。

items.example: The old road underlay the new town.
items.exampleCN: 那条老街躺在新的小镇下面。

items.example: The field is underlain by chalk.
items.exampleCN: 这片旷野以白垩层为底。

items.meaning: existing as a hidden cause or basis
items.example: The underlying idea is simple.
items.exampleCN: 背后的理念其实很简单。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词或名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing makes underlying usable as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 让 underlying 能当形容词用。

items.meaning: to draw a line under or to stress
items.example: Underline the main point.
items.exampleCN: 把要点画上线。

items.meaning: a person or firm that agrees to cover losses
items.example: The underwriter accepted the risk.
items.exampleCN: 承保人接受了这个风险。

latinEntries.meaning: to throw or to lay down
latinEntries.meaningCN: 投掷；躺下（仅作对照，并非本词的出处）

latinEntries.meaning: to lie under, to be at hand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 躺在下面；处于……之下（结构上类似，但与本词无直接传递关系）

definition_zh: 下属；小人物；地位较低、受人差遣的人
definition_en: a person of low rank who must obey someone more powerful, used to stress how unimportant or dependent that person is
core_image: 层层台阶的最下一级站着一个人，抬头等着上面的人吩咐
scene: 公司并购后，只有经理被叫进会议室，文件一分，他就得挨个通知每一个人。The manager made it clear that the decisions were his, and everyone else in the office was just an underling.
sceneCN: 这里 underling 是「地位低下、受人差遣的下属」（第 1 个义项：地位低、只能听命于上级的人）；句意为经理明说决定由他来做，办公室里其他人不过是被差遣的下属。

pos.zh: 下属；小人物；助手

derivatives.zh: 构成这个词的前缀来源，义为「在……之下」
罕用，由 underling 加 -ish 构成，义为「下属式的；谄媚服从的」
由同样以 under 打头的复合方式构成，义为「底层群体」，可作同构参照

senses.title: A person of low rank who obeys others
senses.definition: an employee or assistant who has very little power and is expected to follow orders
senses.definitionCN: 权力很小、只被要求服从命令的雇员或助手
senses.example: The director sent one of his underlings to fetch the files.
senses.exampleCN: 主任派了一个下属去取文件。
senses.why: Under names the position below, and the -ling ending once marked a person, so the word started as the person who stands under another in a hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: under 指明「在下面」的位置，而 -ling 曾经是表示「人」的词尾，所以这个词一开始就是指层级里站在别人下面的人。

senses.title: An unimportant figure in a plot or power game
senses.titleCN: 小人物；（权力游戏中的）小卒
senses.definition: a minor figure who carries out the wishes of someone stronger, used mainly to show that the person matters very little
senses.definitionCN: 替强者办事的小角色，用法主要在于说明这个人无足轻重
senses.example: The film villain does the talking while his underlings do the work.
senses.exampleCN: 电影里的反派负责说话，干活的都是他的小跟班。
senses.why: From office rank the word travels to crime stories and politics, where the person who obeys is simply a small piece of a larger scheme.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从办公室的层级走进犯罪故事与政治较量的叙事里，此时服从的人只是大局面里的一小块。

senses.title: A person put down for their low status
senses.definition: a word used to put someone down, suggesting that the person is only a follower with no authority
senses.definitionCN: 用来压低对方的说法，暗示此人只是个没有权威的跟从者
senses.example: He resented being treated like an underling by visiting officials.
senses.exampleCN: 他讨厌被来访的官员当成小跟班对待。
senses.why: The hierarchy image carries a sting: describing someone as an underling says more about contempt than about the job itself, which is why careful writers use it with care.
senses.whyCN: 那种层级画面自带一根刺：称别人为 underling，表达的多半是轻蔑而不是职位的实事，因此谨慎的写作者会小心使用。

intro.en: Underling is formed inside English from the preposition under and the suffix -ling, which once made nouns for people, as in hireling and earthling; it is not a borrowed Latin word.
intro.cn: underling 是英语内部构词的结果：介词 under 加上曾经专门造「人」的 -ling 后缀，类似 hireling、earthling；它不是从拉丁语借来的词。

items.en: Under is a native Old English preposition meaning below, and the -ling suffix is a native noun-forming ending of great age.
items.cn: under 是本土古英语介词，意为「在下面」，而 -ling 后缀也来自本土的构名词尾。

items.en: In hireling and earthling the suffix marks a person connected to something, not a small object.
items.cn: 这个后缀标出的是与另一人或另一物相关的人，而不是小东西。

items.en: Middle English underling already names a subordinate, and the word keeps that rank sense from its first appearances.
items.cn: 中古英语 underling 已经指「下属」，从最初出现时就带着这个层级意义。

items.en: The older use also covered a person with no official rank, and today the word leans towards contempt.
items.cn: 较早的用法也泛指没有正式职位的人，今天这个词更多带轻蔑色彩。

items.en: Modern reporting uses the plural underlings for the people who obey a powerful figure, often in crime, politics, or office stories.
items.cn: 现代报道常用复数指那些听命于强者的人，多见于犯罪、政治或职场故事。

note.en: The first group gathers the words that share under or the -ling ending; the second gathers the ordinary words for a person who works under someone else.
note.cn: 第一组是含有 under 或 -ling 的形近词；第二组是表示「在别人手下做事的人」的普通词。

entries.definition: to sell cheaper than someone or to weaken them
entries.definitionCN: 以低价抢生意；削弱。同样以 under 开头，后半部分与词源都不同

entries.definition: to draw a line under words or to stress a point
entries.definitionCN: 在下面画线；强调。只是同以 under 开头，后半部分与词源都不同

entries.definition: to weaken something bit by bit from below
entries.definitionCN: 暗中削弱。同样以 under 开头，但后半部分来自「矿」，词源不同

entries.definition: a young duck
entries.definitionCN: 小鸭；这里 -ling 指「小的」，与指「人」的用法虽同源却已不同

entries.definition: a person who works only for pay
entries.definitionCN: 只为报酬干活的人；同一个 -ling 词尾造出的另一个指人词

entries.definition: a person of lower rank in an organisation
entries.definitionCN: 下级；下属，语气中性、正式，不带轻蔑

entries.definition: a follower who obeys without question
entries.definitionCN: 仆从；跟班，明显带轻蔑或戏谑

entries.definition: a person who helps someone with their work
a person who flatters and serves a powerful person
entries.definitionCN: 谄媚的随从；走狗，轻蔑程度更明显

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the under- prefix, the -ling suffix, and the ordinary collocations; the abstract hooks see a figure on the lowest step of a stair.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 under- 前缀、-ling 后缀和常用搭配；抽象记忆点想象站在台阶最下面一级的人。

normal.en: Under- means below, and -ling once made words for people, so the word is a person placed below.
normal.cn: under- 表示在下面，-ling 曾经造人与物的名词：合起来就是一个被放在下面的人。

normal.en: A hireling is a person hired only for pay, which shows the suffix marking a person rather than a small thing.
normal.cn: hireling 是只为报酬受雇的人，可见这个后缀标的是「人」，而不只是「小」。

normal.en: Hireling, earthling and duckling all carry the same ending and show what it builds: a person or thing joined to another.
normal.cn: hireling、earthling 与 duckling 都带同一个词尾，可以看出它造的是「与另一项相关的人或物」。

normal.en: Compare underling with subordinate: the first carries contempt, the second is neutral office language.
normal.cn: 对比 underling 与 subordinate：前者带轻蔑，后者是中性的职场用语。

normal.en: In stories the plural underlings usually means the people who carry out a villain plan.
normal.cn: 在故事里，复数形式通常指负责执行反派计划的那群人。

abstract.en: Picture a stair with a name on every step, and the smallest name at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一排台阶，每一级都写着一个名字，最下面那级的名字最小。

abstract.en: Imagine a puppeteer whose strings run down to small hands below.
abstract.cn: 想象一个提线木偶师，线一直垂到下方那些小手上。

abstract.en: Think of the queue at a service desk: one person hands the ticket down the line.
abstract.cn: 想象服务台前的队伍：一个人把号票沿着队伍往下传。

examples.en: Senior managers rarely mix with the underlings who do the daily work.
examples.cn: 高层管理者很少与那些干日常活儿的下属来往。

examples.en: The politician let his underlings face the journalists while he slipped out the back.
examples.cn: 那位政客让下属去应付记者，自己从后门溜走了。

examples.en: She was tired of being treated as an underling in her own department.
examples.cn: 她厌倦了在自己部门里被当成小跟班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安定凌」——被「安」在「定」好的底层，还得听「凌」驾于其上的人，就是下属；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 本土 under（在下面）+ 本土后缀 -ling（构成与某事物相关的人或物，如 hireling、earthling）→ 中古英语 underling「下属」；现代多带轻蔑色彩。

sensesIntro.en: Underling begins with a rank below another, widens to a small figure in a plot or power game, and finally takes on a tone that puts the person down.
sensesIntro.cn: underling 从「排在别人下面的职位」开始，扩大到权力游戏中的小角色，最后变得更像在贬低所指之人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing on the lowest step of a stair, waiting to be told what to do.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在台阶最下一级，等着上面的人吩咐。

branches.en: RANK: the office sense has no insult in itself, and it only records who stands below whom.
branches.cn: 层级：职场义本身不带侮辱，只是记录谁站在谁的下面。

branches.en: PLOT: in crime and politics the same person shrinks into a small piece of a larger scheme.
branches.cn: 剧情：在犯罪与政治故事里，同一种人缩小成大计划里的一小块。

branches.en: STING: calling a person an underling mainly says that the speaker looks down on them.
branches.cn: 刺痛：把某人叫作 underling，主要是说说话人看不起对方。

branches.en: The office scene and the insult share one picture, an observer who reads rank as worth.
branches.cn: 职场画面与侮辱共享同一幅图：旁观者把层级读成了价值。

branches.en: A small figure in a story is exactly the kind of person the sting is aimed at.
branches.cn: 故事里的那个小角色，正是那根轻蔑的刺所要指向的人。

intro.en: Underling joins the native prefix under- and the native suffix -ling; both halves are English, so there is no Latin root to trace.
intro.cn: underling 由本土前缀 under- 与本土后缀 -ling 拼成，两部分都是英语自身的东西，因此没有拉丁词根可追溯。

latinIntro.en: Because under and -ling are both native, Latin contributes nothing to this word; the couple of Latin entries below are listed only as distant companions for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: 由于 under 与 -ling 都是本土成分，拉丁语对这个词没有贡献；下面屈指可数的拉丁条目只作为远亲对照列出。

items.example: The prefix under- marks the lower rank.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 标出较低的等级。

items.meaning: forming a person or thing connected with something
items.meaningCN: 构成与某事相关的人或物的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ling turns hire into hireling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ling 把 hire 变成 hireling。

items.example: Underling names the person lowest on the ladder.
items.exampleCN: underling 指梯子上位置最低的那个人。

items.example: His underlings did all the talking.
items.exampleCN: 说话的全是他的下属。

items.meaning: someone who works only for money
items.meaningCN: 雇佣兵式的人；只为钱干活的人
items.example: A hireling is suspected of loyalty only to pay.
items.exampleCN: 人们总怀疑 hireling 只忠诚于报酬。

items.example: Sibling ends in a similar person-making ending.
items.exampleCN: sibling 的结尾是一个相近的造「人」词尾。

items.meaning: a creature that lives on earth
items.example: Earthling is used in science fiction.
items.exampleCN: earthling 多用在科幻作品里。

items.example: A duckling is small and young.
items.exampleCN: duckling 指又小又年轻的鸭子。

items.meaning: people below the class of ordinary workers
items.example: Underclass names a whole social group, not one person.
items.exampleCN: underclass 指一整个下层群体，而不是一个人。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 在下面（与 under 语义相近，但并非本词的构词成分）
构成指小名词的后缀（与 -ling 只是在功能上相似）

definition_zh: 支撑；加固（结构）；构成（论点、制度）的基础；支持
definition_en: to support something from below, or to form the basis that keeps an idea, system, or argument firm
core_image: 一根木柱顶在墙根下，从底面把整面墙托住
scene: 老石桥的桥墩裂了缝，工人搬来一根木柱从桥底顶住。Workers pushed a wooden prop under the cracked pier and began to underpin the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 underpin 是「从下面支撑、加固」（第 1 个义项：在结构下方加固）；句意：工人们把一根木顶撑塞到开裂的桥墩下，开始加固这座桥。

pos.zh: 支撑；加固；构成……的基础；支持

derivatives.zh: 基础；支柱；支撑结构
有根基支撑的
销子；别针

senses.title: To prop up a structure
senses.definition: to support a wall, bridge, or building from below with a prop or new foundation
senses.definitionCN: 用支撑物或新地基从下方托住墙、桥或建筑
senses.example: Engineers underpinned the old chapel with steel beams.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用钢梁加固了那座古老的小教堂。
senses.why: The word is built from under plus pin, so the core picture is something driven in low and holding the weight above.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 under 与 pin 组成，核心画面是把东西从下方钉进去、托住上面的重量。

senses.title: To form the basis of
senses.definition: to act as the foundation on which something larger depends
senses.definitionCN: 充当更大的事物所依赖的基础
senses.example: Small firms underpin the local economy.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业支撑着当地经济。
senses.why: A prop hidden under a wall becomes a metaphor for anything that quietly carries a whole system.
senses.whyCN: 藏在墙下的支撑物，被用来比喻默默承载整套体系的事物。

senses.title: To give firm support to an argument
senses.definition: to strengthen a claim, belief, or set of facts with solid evidence or backing
senses.definitionCN: 用确凿证据或支持使主张、信念或事实更牢固
senses.example: The new data underpin the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 新数据为这一理论提供了支撑。
senses.why: Evidence plays the role of the prop that plants the argument firmly in place.
senses.whyCN: 证据扮演支撑物的角色，把论点稳稳地固定住。

senses.title: To be the physical cause behind an effect
senses.definition: to be the process or condition that causes an observed effect, as in science and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 作为引起所观察效应的过程或条件，常见于科学与医学
senses.example: A slow leak may underpin the rising damp in the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的渗漏可能是地窖返潮的成因。
senses.why: What lies beneath is the hidden cause, so the supporting prop becomes the unseen process behind an effect.
senses.whyCN: 位于下方的东西就是隐藏的成因，于是作为支撑的底柱变成了效应背后的隐形过程。

senses.title: To shore up confidence or morale
senses.definition: to keep a mood, group, or market from collapsing by steady support
senses.definitionCN: 以稳定支持使情绪、群体或市场不致崩塌
senses.example: Steady wages underpin public confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 稳定的工资托住了公众的信心。
senses.why: A prop keeps a sagging wall upright, so underpin can hold up fragile things such as confidence.
senses.whyCN: 支撑物让下陷的墙保持直立，因此 underpin 也能撑住信心这类脆弱之物。

intro.en: Underpin joins under with pin, a small wooden peg or metal nail, recorded in the past participle form from the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: underpin 由 under 与 pin（小木栓、金属钉）组合而成，从十六世纪起以过去分词形式见诸文献。

items.en: Pinnare, a verb from pinna, means to fix with a pin or peg.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinnare（源自 pinna）意为用钉或木栓固定。

items.en: Under already means beneath, and pinn is a peg.
items.cn: 古英语 under 已表示在下方，pinn 表示木栓。

items.en: Underpinned appears in building records for a wall held from below.
items.cn: 十六世纪的建筑记载里出现 underpinned，指从下方托住的墙。

items.en: The verb spreads from masonry to arguments and economic foundations.
items.cn: 这个词从砌体工程扩展到论点与经济基础。

items.en: Modern English says that a system is underpinned by facts or funding.
items.cn: 现代英语常说某体系以事实或资金作为基础。

note.en: Underpin is built on under and pin; its neighbours describe forms of support, from buildings to arguments.
note.cn: underpin 建立在 under 与 pin 之上；它的邻词都是不同形式的「支撑」，从建筑到论点。

entries.definition: a thin piece of metal used to fasten things
directly below something
to weaken something gradually from below
entries.definitionCN: 从下方逐层削弱；暗中破坏

entries.definition: to hold something up and stop it falling
to make a structure or idea stronger
to prop something up with a strut

normalIntro.en: Underpin is a picture word: a pin or prop placed under something, holding it from beneath.
normalIntro.cn: underpin 是个画面词：在底下放一根钉或撑杆，从下方托住。

normal.en: Under means beneath and pin means peg, so the peg goes under the weight.
normal.cn: under 表示下方，pin 表示木栓，木栓塞在重量之下。

normal.en: Passive form be underpinned by is common for bases and evidence.
normal.cn: 被动形式 be underpinned by 常用于基础与证据。

normal.en: Remember its twin undermine: one supports below, the other weakens below.
normal.cn: 记住它的双胞胎 undermine：一个在下方支撑，一个在下方削弱。

normal.en: Building reports say the pier was underpinned with concrete.
normal.cn: 工程记录会说桥墩用混凝土加固，用的是 underpinned。

normal.en: Compare support: support is general, underpin is formal and usually says what lies beneath.
normal.cn: 对比 support：support 更泛，underpin 较正式，通常强调底下有什么在承托。

abstract.en: Imagine a wooden post jammed beneath a sagging beam.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木柱顶在下沉的大梁下面。

abstract.en: Think of a foundation stone hidden under a tall tower.
abstract.cn: 想象高楼脚下那块被遮住的基石。

abstract.en: Picture data acting as pillars under a shaky theory.
abstract.cn: 想象数据像柱子一样撑在摇晃的理论下面。

examples.en: Steel beams were used to underpin the sagging walls.
examples.cn: 人们用钢梁加固了下沉的墙体。

examples.en: Trust is the quality that underpins every long partnership.
examples.cn: 信任是支撑每一段长久合作关系的品质。

examples.en: The study is underpinned by ten years of field records.
examples.cn: 这项研究以十年的野外记录作为基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「按得平」——把支柱按得平平的、稳稳顶在下面，就是支撑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: un-（下）+ pin（销子、木栓）→ 在下面钉入销子，从底面托住 → 引申为「构成基础、支持」。

sensesIntro.en: Underpin starts as a builder word for propping a wall from below, then spreads to economics, arguments, causes, and confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: underpin 起初是建筑行话，指从下方托住墙体，后来扩展到经济、论点、成因与信心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a post pushed under a wall to hold it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根木柱顶在墙下把墙托住。

branches.en: The literal building sense keeps the physical prop.
branches.cn: 字面的建筑义项保留实体支撑物。

branches.en: The basis sense moves the prop into a system.
branches.cn: 基础义项把支撑物移入体系之中。

branches.en: The argument sense uses evidence as the prop.
branches.cn: 论点义项把证据当作支撑物。

branches.en: Hidden causes and fragile moods are both things held from below.
branches.cn: 隐藏成因而脆弱的情绪，都是从下方被托住的东西。

branches.en: A bridge pier and an economy are both kept standing by support beneath.
branches.cn: 桥墩与经济一样，都靠下方的支撑才立得住。

intro.en: Underpin combines the prefix under with the noun pin, and the family grows towards underpinning and undermine.
intro.cn: underpin 由前缀 under 与名词 pin 组合而成，词族向 underpinning、undermine 延伸。

latinIntro.en: The pin element traces back to Latin pinna, a peg, which also gives English pin.
latinIntro.cn: pin 这一成分可追溯到拉丁语 pinna（木栓），英语 pin 也由此而来。

items.example: Under- places the action beneath something.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 表示动作发生在某物下方。

items.meaning: a peg or thin metal fastener
items.example: Pin gives the fastening image.
items.exampleCN: pin 提供固定的意象。

items.example: Underpin is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: underpin 是基本动词。

items.example: The underpinned wall holds firm.
items.exampleCN: 加固过的墙很稳固。

items.example: The underpinning gives the system its base.
items.exampleCN: 支撑结构给体系提供基础。

items.example: Undermine is the opposite partner.
items.exampleCN: undermine 是相对的反向词。

items.example: Reinforce is a near neighbour.
items.exampleCN: reinforce 是近邻词。

items.example: Shore up names the same prop action.
items.exampleCN: shore up 表达同样的支撑动作。

items.meaning: forms nouns of action or result
items.meaningCN: 构成动作或结果名词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms underpinning.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 underpinning。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms underpinned.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 underpinned。

definition_zh: 可以理解的；合乎情理的；（语言、表达）易懂的
definition_en: easy to understand and think reasonable, or able to be understood by someone
core_image: 一片迷雾散开，前面的路一眼就看得清清楚楚
scene: 她迟到了半小时，浑身湿透，说是公交抛了锚，大家听了都点头。She was half an hour late and soaked through, so her excuse was understandable.
sceneCN: 这里 understandable 是「合乎情理的、可以体谅的」（第 2 个义项：可以理解并值得同情）；句意：她迟到了半小时还浑身湿透，所以她的解释是情有可原的。

pos.zh: 可以理解的；合乎情理的；易懂的

derivatives.zh: 理解；明白了
可以理解地；难怪
理解；谅解
误解；误会

senses.title: Easy to grasp
senses.definition: clear enough to be understood without much effort
senses.definitionCN: 足够清楚，不必费多大力气就能明白
senses.example: The guide is written in plain, understandable English.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南用浅显易懂的英语写成。
senses.why: The adjective adds -able to understand, so the word first means able to be understood by a reader or listener.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是在 understand 后加 -able，所以首要义项是「能被读者或听者明白」的。

senses.title: Reasonable and forgivable
senses.definition: natural or reasonable in the situation, so that nobody can blame it
senses.definitionCN: 在当时情境下自然、合理，让人无从责怪
senses.example: Her nervousness was completely understandable.
senses.exampleCN: 她的紧张完全可以理解。
senses.why: If a cause is clear to the mind, the mind also accepts it, so clear to grasp slides into fair enough to excuse.
senses.whyCN: 若原因在头脑中清楚可见，心里也就容易接受，于是「易懂」滑向「情有可原」。

senses.title: Able to be followed from context
senses.definition: possible for another person to follow or recognize from the words, sounds, or signs used
senses.definitionCN: 别人能凭所用的词语、声音或信号听明白、看明白
senses.example: Her accent was thick but still understandable.
senses.exampleCN: 她的口音很重，但还是听得懂。
senses.why: Even when speech is rough, the hearer can still stand under the meaning, so the sense stays close to the base verb.
senses.whyCN: 即便说得粗糙，听者仍能站到意义的下面去，因此这一义项紧贴基本动词。

intro.en: Understandable is understand plus -able, and the verb itself comes from stand in the sense of standing under or among a matter.
intro.cn: understandable 由 understand 加 -able 构成，而动词 understand 来自 stand（站立），意为站到事情的下方或其中。

items.en: Understand appears early in English as forstandan and understandan, with the sense of standing in the middle of something.
items.cn: 古英语早期就有 under- 与 standan 的组合，意为站到某事之中，掌握其来龙去脉。

items.en: The form understand settles in place and names grasping someone else.
items.cn: understand 这一形式固定下来，指领会别人的意思。

items.en: The suffix -able comes from Latin habilis, meaning that can be held or handled.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 来自拉丁语 habilis，意为可以被握住、被处理。

items.en: Understandable forms as able to be understood.
items.cn: understandable 出现，意为能被理解的。

items.en: The adjective gains the everyday sense of reasonable and forgivable.
items.cn: 这个形容词获得了「合乎情理、情有可原」的日常义项。

note.en: Understandable belongs to the understand family and stands beside words for clear and for forgivable.
note.cn: understandable 属于 understand 词族，并与「清楚」类与「宽恕」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to know the meaning of something
the ability to grasp meaning, or sympathy
in a way that can be understood
able to be understood by the mind
easy to see, hear, or grasp
shown to be reasonable or right

normalIntro.en: Understandable carries the whole understand family on its back: the verb, the noun, and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: understandable 背负着整个 understand 词族：动词、名词与副词。

normal.en: The suffix -able means that can be done, so understandable means that can be understood.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 表示「能够被……」，所以 understandable 就是「能够被理解的」。

normal.en: The adverb understandably means in a way one can understand, and it opens many sentences.
normal.cn: 副词 understandably 表示可以理解地，常用于句首。

normal.en: It is understandable that is a very common frame in speaking tests.
normal.cn: 「it is understandable that」是口语考试中很常见的句式。

normal.en: Remember the opposite side: the prefix mis- in misunderstand means wrongly.
normal.cn: 记住反方向：misunderstand 中的前缀 mis- 表示错误地。

normal.en: Compare comprehensible: comprehensible is formal and about difficulty, while understandable also works for fairness.
normal.cn: 对比 comprehensible：它更正式、侧重难度；understandable 还能表示情理上说得通。

abstract.en: Picture fog lifting so that the path ahead is plain to see.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气散开，前面的路一清二楚。

abstract.en: Think of hearing a friend explain a silly fear and nodding at once.
abstract.cn: 想象听朋友说出一个小小的恐惧，你立刻点头。

abstract.en: Imagine a muffled voice on a phone that still comes through in the end.
abstract.cn: 想象电话里闷闷的声音，最后仍然听得清楚。

examples.en: The manual uses short sentences that are understandable to beginners.
examples.cn: 这本手册用初学者也能看懂的短句写成。

examples.en: It is understandable that parents worry about screen time.
examples.cn: 父母担心屏幕使用时间是可以理解的。

examples.en: Given the storm, a delay seemed completely understandable.
examples.cn: 考虑到暴风雨，延误看起来完全情有可原。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德斯坦的波」——安德站在斯坦讲的那道波旁，听懂了，所以是可理解的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: under（在下）+ stand（站立）→ 站到事情下面，弄清来龙去脉 → understand（理解）；加后缀 -able（能够被……的）→ understandable（能被理解的 → 合乎情理的）。

sensesIntro.en: Understandable moves from a text that can be grasped, to a cause or person that can be excused, to speech that can still be followed.
sensesIntro.cn: understandable 从「能被读懂的文本」，走到「可以体谅的原因或人」，再到「仍然能被跟上的话」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fog clearing so that the path is easy to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾气散开，路一眼就能看清。

branches.en: A clear text is the basic able-to-be-understood sense.
branches.cn: 清楚的文本是最基本的「能被理解」义项。

branches.en: Something clearly causeable also becomes forgivable.
branches.cn: 原因显而易见的事，也就变得情有可原。

branches.en: Speech that can be followed keeps the base verb close by.
branches.cn: 能够被跟上听懂的话，最贴近基本动词。

branches.en: Written clarity and spoken clarity both let the listener stand under the meaning.
branches.cn: 书面清楚与口头清楚，都让听者能够站到意义的下面。

branches.en: When we follow a reason and hear the full story, we tend to forgive.
branches.cn: 当我们听懂来龙去脉、听完整段故事，往往就会体谅。

intro.en: Understandable is built on the verb understand plus the suffix -able, with understanding and misunderstand nearby.
intro.cn: understandable 由动词 understand 加后缀 -able 构成，近旁的词还有 understanding 与 misunderstand。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -able comes from Latin habilis, able to be held, and stand shares a deep root with Latin stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -able 源自拉丁语 habilis（能被握住的），stand 与拉丁语 stare（站立）共享更古老的词根。

items.example: Under- gives the image of standing within a matter.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 under- 给出站在事情之中的画面。

items.example: Stand gives the verb its spine.
items.exampleCN: stand 给这个词提供骨架。

items.example: Understand is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: understand 是基本动词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms understandable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 understandable。

items.example: Understandable is the target word.
items.exampleCN: understandable 是目标词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms understandably.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 understandably。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms understanding.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 understanding。

items.example: The prefix mis- forms misunderstand.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mis- 构成 misunderstand。

items.example: Comprehend is a formal near neighbour.
items.exampleCN: comprehend 是正式语体的近邻词。

items.example: Comprehensible rivals understandable in formal prose.
items.exampleCN: 在正式文章里 comprehensible 与它互为近义词。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be held or handled

definition_zh: 未被察觉的；未被发现的；未被检测出的
definition_en: not noticed, found, or recognized, usually because something stays hidden from attention or testing
core_image: 一个人躲在幕布后，灯光扫过去却什么也没照到
scene: 老鼠在仓库角落里啃着粮袋，看守人提灯走过却没有发现。The mice ate through the grain sacks and stayed undetected behind the crates.
sceneCN: 这里 undetected 是「未被察觉的」（第 1 个义项：没被人注意到）；句意：老鼠啃穿了粮袋，一直藏在板条箱后面没被发现。

pos.zh: 未被察觉的；未被发现的；未被检测出的

derivatives.zh: 察觉；发现；探测
发现；侦测
探测器
侦探

senses.title: Going unnoticed by people
senses.definition: not noticed by anyone while moving, acting, or staying in place
senses.definitionCN: 在行动或停留时没有被任何人注意到
senses.example: The thief slipped out through the kitchen and went undetected.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷从厨房溜了出去，一路没被发现。
senses.why: The prefix un- flips the past participle of detect, so undetected means detect has simply not happened.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 把 detect 的过去分词翻转，undetected 就是「发现」这个动作从未发生。

senses.title: Not found by testing
senses.definition: present but not revealed by a check, scan, or test
senses.definitionCN: 存在，但未被检查、扫描或测试揭示出来
senses.example: A single undetected error ruined the whole dataset.
senses.exampleCN: 一个未被查出的错误毁掉了整个数据集。
senses.why: Detection is also what instruments do, so undetected covers what passes through a machine or a review unseen.
senses.whyCN: 探测也是仪器在做的事，因此 undetected 也指从机器或审查中溜过去、没被看见的东西。

senses.title: Hidden from scanners and sensors
senses.definition: not registered by a sensor or a medical test, often because it is weak or buried
senses.definitionCN: 未被传感器或医学检查记录下来，常常因为信号太弱或被遮蔽
senses.example: Some early cancers remain undetected for years.
senses.exampleCN: 一些早期癌症多年都未被发现。
senses.why: Small signals that hide under noise share the picture of something moving past a lit stage unseen.
senses.whyCN: 藏在噪声下面的微弱信号，与从灯光下溜过去却未被看见的画面相通。

intro.en: Undetected is un- plus the past participle of detect, and detect comes from Latin detegere, to uncover.
intro.cn: undetected 由 un- 加 detect 的过去分词构成，而 detect 来自拉丁语 detegere，意为揭开覆盖。

items.en: Detegere combines de- away and tegere to cover, so it means to remove the cover.
items.cn: detegere 由 de-（去掉）与 tegere（遮盖）组成，意为揭开覆盖。

items.en: Detect enters English meaning to uncover or reveal what is hidden.
items.cn: detect 进入英语时意为揭露、暴露被掩盖的东西。

items.en: The verb shifts towards noticing what was concealed.
items.cn: 这个词转向指察觉被隐藏的事物。

items.en: Undetected forms from un- plus the past participle.
items.cn: undetected 由前缀 un- 加过去分词构成。

items.en: Scientific and police senses give the adjective a broad technical range.
items.cn: 科学探测与警务侦查的用法让这个形容词拥有宽广的技术用法。

items.en: Modern English uses it for errors, disease, and secret passage.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述错误、疾病与秘密穿行。

note.en: Undetected is the negative of detected and sits among words for things that stay hidden.
note.cn: undetected 是 detected 的反面，并与一批表示「保持隐藏」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to notice or find something hidden
the act of finding something
a device that finds signals
not found or learned yet
not observed by anyone
kept out of sight

normalIntro.en: Undetected is a switch on detect: un- turns the uncovering off and leaves the thing still under its cover.
normalIntro.cn: undetected 是 detect 的开关：un- 把「揭开」关掉，东西还盖在里面。

normal.en: The prefix un- negates the past participle, so undetected means never detected.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 否定过去分词，所以 undetected 就是「从未被发现」。

normal.en: It mostly follows verbs such as go, remain, and escape.
normal.cn: 它多跟在 go、remain、escape 这类动词后面。

normal.en: The adjective is shared with Latin tegere, to cover, as in a protective cover.
normal.cn: 这个词与拉丁语 tegere（遮盖）同源，就像一层保护性覆盖物。

normal.en: Note the family: detect, detection, detector, detective.
normal.cn: 记住词族：detect、detection、detector、detective。

normal.en: Compare unnoticed: unnoticed is social, undetected is technical or stealthy.
normal.cn: 对比 unnoticed：unnoticed 偏人际，undetected 偏技术或隐秘。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow crossing a lit stage and the light never finding it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子穿过亮着的舞台，灯光始终没找到它。

abstract.en: Think of a tiny typo slipping past every proofreader.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小错字从每位校对员眼前溜过。

abstract.en: Imagine a faint signal buried under hospital noise.
abstract.cn: 想象医院的噪声里埋着一个微弱的信号。

examples.en: The leak went undetected for almost a month.
examples.cn: 这处渗漏将近一个月都没被发现。

examples.en: Undetected faults can crash a whole system later.
examples.cn: 未被检出的故障日后可能让整个系统崩溃。

examples.en: Some viruses spread while remaining undetected in carriers.
examples.cn: 有些病毒在携带者体内未被察觉时就已传播。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的台克替的」——盗贼「安」装好后「替」掉痕迹，无人察觉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: un-（不、未）+ detect（发现，来自拉丁语 de-（去掉）+ tegere（遮盖））+ -ed → 遮盖未被揭开 → undetected（未被发现的）。

sensesIntro.en: Undetected starts with people slipping past notice, then spreads to errors that pass a check and signals that a sensor misses.
sensesIntro.cn: undetected 先从人从他人眼皮下溜过开始，再扩展到通过检查的错误和逃过仪器的信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shadow slipping past the light unseen.
core.cn: 核心意象：影子在灯光下溜过却没被看见。

branches.en: A person who moves unseen is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 行动未被看见的人，是这个词的朴素义项。

branches.en: A flaw passing inspection is the testing sense.
branches.cn: 通不过检查的缺陷是检测义项。

branches.en: A buried signal is the sensor sense.
branches.cn: 埋在底下的信号是传感器义项。

branches.en: Both a stealthy visitor and a silent bug stay under cover.
branches.cn: 潜行的来客与沉默的漏洞，都躲在遮掩之下。

branches.en: Tests and sensors both fail to lift the cover, so both leave things undetected.
branches.cn: 测试与传感器都没揭开那层遮盖，于是两者都让事物保持未被发现。

intro.en: Undetected is built from the negating prefix un-, the verb detect, and the participle ending -ed.
intro.cn: undetected 由否定前缀 un-、动词 detect 与分词词尾 -ed 组成。

latinIntro.en: Detect goes back to Latin detegere, from de- and tegere, to cover.
latinIntro.cn: detect 可追溯到拉丁语 detegere，由 de- 与 tegere（遮盖）构成。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the action.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定这一动作。

items.example: De- means the cover is taken away.
items.exampleCN: de- 表示把遮盖拿走。

items.example: Tegere gives the covering image.
items.exampleCN: tegere 提供遮覆的意象。

items.example: Detect is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: detect 是基本动词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms detected.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 detected。

items.example: Undetected is the target word.
items.exampleCN: undetected 是目标词。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms detection.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 detection。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -or forms detector.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 detector。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms detective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 detective。

items.example: Unnoticed is the social twin of undetected.
items.exampleCN: unnoticed 是它在人际层面的双胞胎。

definition_zh: 未开发的；未发展的；不发达的；未显影的
definition_en: not yet developed, built on, or brought to full growth
core_image: 一块空白的土地，上面还没有任何建筑和道路
scene: 考察队走进山谷深处的荒原，放眼望去只有泥土和野草。The expedition crossed a vast stretch of undeveloped land with no roads at all.
sceneCN: 这里 undeveloped 是「未开发的」（第 1 个义项：土地还没有被开发建设）；句意：考察队穿过了一大片没有任何道路的未开发土地。

pos.zh: 未开发的；未发展的
（照片）未显影的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加名词后缀 -ness，义为「未开发的状态」
去掉否定前缀 un- 后的动词本义「发展；开发」
develop 加名词后缀 -ment，义为「发展；开发」

senses.title: Land not yet built on or used
senses.definition: describing land or an area that has not been built on, farmed, or put to practical use
senses.definitionCN: 指土地或地区还没有被建设、耕作或实际利用
senses.example: The council wants to keep the riverbank undeveloped.
senses.exampleCN: 议会希望让河岸保持未开发状态。
senses.why: The un- prefix cancels the development that develop implies, so the land is pictured before any building starts.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 un- 抵消了 develop 所暗示的「开发」，于是画面停留在动工之前的那块空地。

senses.title: A country or region that lags in growth
senses.definition: describing an economy or region that has not yet reached modern industrial or social growth
senses.definitionCN: 指经济或地区还没有达到现代工业或社会发展的水平
senses.example: Many undeveloped regions lack clean water and roads.
senses.exampleCN: 许多不发达地区缺乏干净的水和道路。
senses.why: Once the image shifts from a plot of land to a whole nation, the same blank picture becomes a measure of how little has been built.
senses.whyCN: 当画面从一块地扩大到整个国家，这幅「空白」的图就变成了衡量建设有多少的标尺。

senses.title: A skill or idea not yet brought out
senses.definition: describing a talent, idea, or resource that exists but has not been cultivated or turned into something useful
senses.definitionCN: 指存在但还没有被培养或转化为有用成果的才能、想法或资源
senses.example: The young writer has real but undeveloped talent.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻作家有真正但尚未发展的才华。
senses.why: Something can be present yet dormant; un- adds the sense that growth has not started, as a seed still in dry soil.
senses.whyCN: 事物可以存在却处于休眠状态；un- 强调生长还没开始，就像种子仍埋在干土里。

senses.title: Photographic film not yet treated
senses.definition: describing film or a photographic image that has been exposed but not yet treated with chemicals to make the picture visible
senses.definitionCN: 指胶片或照片已经曝光，但还没有经过化学处理使影像显现出来
senses.example: The negatives were still undeveloped after years in a drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 这些底片在抽屉里放了多年，仍未显影。
senses.why: Development in photography means letting the hidden image come out; an undeveloped film keeps the picture invisible.
senses.whyCN: 摄影中的显影就是让隐藏的影像浮现，未显影的胶片则把画面一直藏在底片上。

intro.en: Undeveloped is the adjective developed with the negative prefix un-, from Old French desveloper, to unwrap.
intro.cn: undeveloped 是形容词 developed 加否定前缀 un-，而 developed 源自法语 desveloper（解开、展开）。

items.en: The base is Latin volvere, to roll or wrap up, which also gives volume and revolve.
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 volvere（卷、包裹），英语 volume 与 revolve 也出自这里。

items.en: Desveloper means to unwrap or unfold something wrapped around.
items.cn: 古法语 desveloper 意为把包好的东西解开、展开。

items.en: Develop enters English and widens from unwrapping to gradual growth.
items.cn: develop 进入英语后，词义从「解开包裹」扩展到「逐步生长」。

items.en: Developed is used for growth, building, and photographic image-making.
items.cn: developed 被用于描述生长、建设以及照片的显影。

items.en: Undeveloped fixes the negative image: land, economies, or film still left without growth.
items.cn: undeveloped 固定了反向画面：土地、经济或胶片还没有发展起来。

note.en: Undeveloped sits among un- negatives and opposite growth words, and near words for empty land or weak economies.
note.cn: undeveloped 与各种 un- 否定词和表示「生长」的反义词相邻，也靠近表示空地或落后经济的词。

entries.definition: built upon or advanced in growth
to grow or make something grow
the process of growth or of building
still natural and not damaged by building
entries.definitionCN: 未受破坏的；保持天然的

entries.definition: less advanced than others
land never yet used or cleared

normalIntro.en: Undeveloped is developed with a switch turned off: the growth never happened.
normalIntro.cn: undeveloped 就是给 developed 关掉开关：发展从未发生。

normal.en: The prefix un- marks a simple negation, so undeveloped means not developed.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 表示直接否定，所以 undeveloped 就是「没有发展的」。

normal.en: Develop comes from an old verb meaning to unwrap, so development is an unfolding.
normal.cn: develop 源自意为「解开包裹」的古词，所以发展是逐步展开的过程。

normal.en: Undeveloped land is a plot still covered with soil and grass.
normal.cn: undeveloped land 是仍然只覆着泥土和草的一块地。

normal.en: Undeveloped talent exists but has not been trained.
normal.cn: undeveloped talent 表示存在但未经训练的才华。

normal.en: Compare developed and underdeveloped: underdeveloped stresses too little progress, undeveloped simply stresses none yet.
normal.cn: 对比 developed 与 underdeveloped：后者强调进展不足，undeveloped 只强调还没有开始。

abstract.en: Picture an empty field with a wooden fence and no house.
abstract.cn: 想象一块只有木栅栏、没有房子的空地。

abstract.en: Think of a map where a whole province is drawn in faint grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，整个省份只用浅灰色草草画出。

abstract.en: Imagine a seed lying in dry soil, waiting for its first rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子躺在干土里，等着第一场雨。

examples.en: Large areas of the coast remain undeveloped.
examples.cn: 大片海岸地区仍未开发。

examples.en: Her raw but undeveloped voice impressed the teacher.
examples.cn: 她那尚未发展却质朴的嗓音打动了老师。

examples.en: The old roll of film had stayed undeveloped for decades.
examples.cn: 那卷旧胶片几十年来一直未显影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺地未乐」——俺的这块地还没开始动工，所以叫「未开发的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 否定前缀 un- + developed（发展的）；developed 溯至古法语 desveloper（解开包裹），更早与拉丁语 volvere（卷、包裹）相关，核心义「还没有被展开、发展起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Undeveloped starts with land that has nothing built on it, then widens to a region that lags in growth, a talent that was never trained, and finally a film image not yet brought out.
sensesIntro.cn: undeveloped 先指没有任何建设的土地，再扩展到落后的地区、未被培养的才能，最后指还未显影的胶片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty field with no house and no road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块没有房子也没有道路的空地。

branches.en: The land sense is the most literal: a plot left without building.
branches.cn: 土地义项最直接：一块还没有动工的地。

branches.en: A whole region can be measured by how little has been built.
branches.cn: 整个地区也可以用「建设得很少」来衡量。

branches.en: Ability and ideas can stay dormant like a seed in dry soil.
branches.cn: 能力和想法也会像干土里的种子一样休眠。

branches.en: Photographic development makes a hidden image visible, so an untreated film is literally not yet developed.
branches.cn: 显影让隐藏的影像显现，所以未处理的胶片字面上就是「没显影」。

branches.en: Empty land and a lagging economy share the same blank picture.
branches.cn: 空地与落后经济共享同一幅「空白」的画面。

intro.en: Undeveloped is built from the prefix un-, the verb develop, and the past participle ending -ed, with words like development and developer nearby.
intro.cn: undeveloped 由否定前缀 un-、动词 develop 和过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，旁边还有 development、developer 等同族词。

latinIntro.en: The develop family reaches back through Old French desveloper to Latin volvere, to roll or wrap.
latinIntro.cn: develop 这一族词经古法语 desveloper 上溯到拉丁语 volvere（卷、包裹）。

items.example: The prefix un- turns developed into undeveloped.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 developed 变成 undeveloped。

items.example: Develop is the verb at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: develop 是这一族词的核心动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示已完成或处于某状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed makes the participle developed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成分词 developed。

items.example: Undo shows the same negating prefix un-.
items.exampleCN: undo 展示了同一个否定前缀 un-。

items.example: Undeveloped keeps the plain negative sense.
items.exampleCN: undeveloped 保留了最直接的否定含义。

items.example: Underdeveloped uses under- rather than un-.
items.exampleCN: underdeveloped 用的是 under- 而不是 un-。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms development.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 development。

items.meaning: a person or firm that does
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或公司的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms developer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 developer。

items.example: Unspoiled shares the un- pattern.
items.exampleCN: unspoiled 同理使用 un- 否定。

items.example: Unused land is close to undeveloped land.
items.exampleCN: unused land 与 undeveloped land 意思接近。

definition_zh: 不加掩饰的；毫不掩饰的；露骨的；公开的
definition_en: open and not hidden or covered up, so that feelings or intentions show plainly
core_image: 一个人摘下面具，把真实的脸完全露出来
scene: 听完那番推诿的说辞，屋里的人都露出了不以为然的神情。His undisguised contempt for the scheme was obvious to everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 undisguised 是「不加掩饰的」（第 1 个义项：情感或态度坦然外露）；句意：他对这项计划毫不掩饰的轻蔑，屋里所有人都看得出来。

pos.zh: 不加掩饰的；毫不掩饰的
（刻意）公开的；不伪装的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「不加掩饰地」
去掉否定前缀后为动词「伪装；掩饰」，名词同形
disguise 加 -ed 构成，义为「伪装的；掩饰的」

senses.title: Emotions shown openly
senses.definition: describing a feeling that is clearly visible because the person makes no attempt to hide it
senses.definitionCN: 指某种情感或态度清楚地流露出来，因为当事人根本没有试图隐藏
senses.example: She watched the speech with undisguised delight.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不掩饰地高兴地看着这场演讲。
senses.why: Something disguised is covered by a mask, so undisguised means the mask is off and the face can be read.
senses.whyCN: 被 disguise（伪装）的事物罩着一层面具，undisguised 就是摘下面具，脸完全能被看清。

senses.title: Intentions stated plainly
senses.definition: describing an intention or motive that is stated plainly and not dressed up in nicer words
senses.definitionCN: 指意图或动机直白地说出，没有用更好听的说法加以修饰
senses.example: He made an undisguised attempt to secure the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫不掩饰地想拿下这份合同。
senses.why: Beyond feelings, the word covers aims that are laid bare for everyone to see.
senses.whyCN: 除情感之外，这个词也覆盖那些被摆到明面上、人尽皆知的意图。

senses.title: Absence of pretence in manner
