senses.definition: describing speech or behaviour that is direct and free of pretence or false politeness
senses.definitionCN: 指言谈或举止直截了当，没有虚饰或虚假的客套
senses.example: Her reply was an undisguised no.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答是一个毫不掩饰的「不」。
senses.why: When the mask is off, manners lose their polish, and directness itself becomes the plainest kind of honesty.
senses.whyCN: 面具取下后，客套也失去了修饰，直率本身就是最朴素的一种坦诚。

intro.en: Undisguised is disguised with the negative prefix un-, from Old French desguiser, to change the outward manner.
intro.cn: undisguised 是 disguised 加否定前缀 un-，而 disguised 源自古法语 desguiser（改变外表举止）。

items.en: The root is probably a Germanic word for manner, related to Gothic and Frankish forms.
items.cn: 词根一般认为来自日耳曼语中表示「举止、方式」的词，与哥特语和法兰克语的形式相关。

items.en: Desguiser means to put off the usual manner, and so to alter ones appearance.
items.cn: 古法语 desguiser 意为「脱去平常的举止」，引申为改变外貌。

items.en: Disguise enters English meaning to alter dress or appearance for concealment.
items.cn: disguise 进入英语，指为了掩藏而改变衣着或外貌。

items.en: Disguised widens from dress to hidden feelings and hidden motives.
items.cn: disguised 的用法从衣着扩展到隐藏的情感与隐藏的动机。

items.en: The un- form brings the hidden feeling back into the open.
items.cn: 加上 un- 后，被藏起的情感又被放回到明面上。

note.en: Undisguised lives among un- negatives of disguise, and near words for feelings that cannot be hidden.
note.cn: undisguised 处在 disguise 一族词与各种「藏不住」的表达之间。

entries.definition: to hide a real identity or feeling
hidden by a false appearance
in an open, unhidden way
not hidden or secret
honest and direct in speech
shameless and openly shown
entries.definitionCN: 厚颜无耻的；露骨的；与 undisguised 同义但更不正式

normalIntro.en: Undisguised is the mask taken off: un- removes disguise.
normalIntro.cn: undisguised 是摘下面具：un- 去掉了 disguise。

normal.en: Disguise carries the idea of a changed outward manner, so undisguised is uncompromised appearance.
normal.cn: disguise 本义是改变外在举止，所以 undisguised 就是不经改动的真实样子。

normal.en: The prefix un- negates directly, giving the plain meaning not disguised.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 直接否定，构成最朴素的含义「没有伪装的」。

normal.en: Undisguised contempt means contempt you can see on the face.
normal.cn: undisguised contempt 指脸上看得一清二楚的轻蔑。

normal.en: With undisguised relief is a common phrase for visible relief.
normal.cn: with undisguised relief 是形容「明显松了口气」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Compare undisguised and blatant: undisguised is about a mask removed, blatant about noise and offence.
normal.cn: 对比 blatant：undisguised 侧重「面具拿掉」，blatant 侧重「喧闹刺眼」。

abstract.en: Picture a performer pulling off a paper mask before the audience.
abstract.cn: 想象一位演员在观众面前把纸面具撕下来。

abstract.en: Think of a face whose frown nothing can smooth away.
abstract.cn: 想象一张皱着眉、怎么也抹不平的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine a sign written in capital letters with no wrapper.
abstract.cn: 想象一块用大字写出来、没有包装的告示牌。

examples.en: The manager met the news with undisguised relief.
examples.cn: 经理听到这个消息后毫不掩饰地松了口气。

examples.en: There was undisguised anger in her voice.
examples.cn: 她的声音里带着毫不掩饰的愤怒。

examples.en: Their undisguised aim was to close the smaller firm.
examples.cn: 他们毫不掩饰的目的是关掉那家小公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺的撕盖子的」——把盖子撕开，里面的一切都露出来，所以是「不加掩饰的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 否定前缀 un- + disguised（伪装的）；disguise 源自古法语 desguiser（改变外在举止），词根一般认为来自日耳曼语表「方式、举止」的词，核心义「不罩面具、原样示人」。

sensesIntro.en: Undisguised begins with feelings that show on the face, spreads to intentions stated openly, and ends with a manner that drops all pretence.
sensesIntro.cn: undisguised 从写在脸上的情感开始，扩展到公开摆出的意图，最后落到毫无虚饰的待人方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person pulling off a mask in front of the crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人当众摘下面具。

branches.en: Feelings become visible once the mask is off.
branches.cn: 面具一摘，情感就显露出来。

branches.en: Intentions are laid bare for everyone to read.
branches.cn: 意图被摊开在明面上供人看清。

branches.en: Manners lose their polish and turn blunt.
branches.cn: 客套失去修饰，变得直截了当。

branches.en: A blunt reply and a visible emotion share the same honest surface.
branches.cn: 直白的回答与明显的情感同样共享「坦诚的表面」。

branches.en: Plain intention and plain manner both refuse the disguise of politeness.
branches.cn: 直白的意图与直白的方式都拒绝用礼貌作伪装。

intro.en: Undisguised pairs the negating prefix un- with disguise and its -ed form, plus the adverb undisguisedly.
intro.cn: undisguised 由否定前缀 un- 与 disguise（及其 -ed 形式）构成，另有副词 undisguisedly。

latinIntro.en: Disguise comes from Old French desguiser, and the underlying manner root is usually traced to Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: disguise 源自法语 desguiser，其「举止」词根一般认为来自日耳曼语，因此没有确凿的拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: not, the reversal of an action
items.example: The prefix un- gives undisguised its plain negative sense.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 赋予 undisguised 直接的否定含义。

items.example: Disguise is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: disguise 是这一族词的基础。

items.example: The old prefix dis- carries the idea of putting off a manner.
items.exampleCN: 古前缀 dis- 带有「脱去某状态」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词、表示某种状态
items.example: The suffix -ed forms disguised.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 disguised。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms undisguisedly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 undisguisedly。

items.example: Undisguised is the whole unit.
items.exampleCN: undisguised 是完整的词形。

items.example: Unconcealed works much like undisguised.
items.exampleCN: unconcealed 与 undisguised 用法相近。

items.example: Unmistakable shows the same un- pattern.
items.exampleCN: unmistakable 使用了相同的 un- 构造。

items.meaning: a cover for the face; to hide
items.example: A mask gives the picture behind undisguised.
items.exampleCN: 面具提供了理解 undisguised 的画面。

definition_zh: 毫无疑问的；无可置疑的；确凿的
definition_en: not doubted by anyone, and accepted as certain or true
core_image: 一枚公章稳稳盖在文件上，谁也不需要再去核对
scene: 比赛结束后，观众席上掌声如潮，没有人提出任何异议。Her talent as a pianist is undoubted and will surely grow with time.
sceneCN: 这里 undoubted 是「毫无疑问的」（第 1 个义项：事实或才能被毫无疑义地承认）；句意：她作为钢琴家的才华毋庸置疑，必然还会随时间增长。

pos.zh: 毫无疑问的；无可置疑的
（通前常加 the）无可争议的（人、优势）

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly，义为「毫无疑问地；无疑」
去掉否定前缀后为动词「怀疑」，名词同形
doubt 加 -ful，义为「怀疑的；不确定的」
doubt 加 -less，义为「无疑的」，也可作副词

senses.title: Beyond any doubt
senses.definition: describing a quality or fact that no informed person would question
senses.definitionCN: 指某种品质或事实，任何有判断的人都不会质疑
senses.example: Her skill as a surgeon is undoubted.
senses.exampleCN: 她的外科医术无可置疑。
senses.why: Doubt marks a gap between belief and fact, so adding un- closes the gap and leaves a fact that needs no checking.
senses.whyCN: doubt 是信念与事实之间的缝隙，加上 un- 就是合上这道缝，留下一个不需要再核对的事实。

senses.title: Agreed by everyone
senses.definition: describing something accepted by general agreement rather than by proof alone
senses.definitionCN: 指某事物是凭普遍共识而非仅靠证明而被接受的
senses.example: The undoubted success of the show saved the theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 演出无可争议的成功挽救了这家剧院。
senses.why: The word leans on public consent: no one raises a hand, so the thing quietly becomes common ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词依赖众人的默认：没有人举手反对，事情就悄悄成了共识。

senses.title: The clear best or strongest
senses.titleCN: （加 the）无可争议的；最突出的
senses.definition: used of a person or group whose superiority stands out clearly above all rivals
senses.definitionCN: 用于某个人或团体，其优势明显高出所有对手
senses.example: She is the undoubted star of the new film.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是这部新片中最耀眼的明星。
senses.why: When nobody even bothers to doubt, the highest ranking becomes so plain that it turns into a title.
senses.whyCN: 当无人费心去质疑时，那个最高的位置就清楚得变成了一个称号。

intro.en: Undoubted joins the negative prefix un- to doubted, from Latin dubitare, to waver or be of two minds.
intro.cn: undoubted 是否定前缀 un- 加 doubted，后者源自拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆、拿不定主意）。

items.en: Dubitare means to hesitate, and is related to duo, two, from the picture of being of two minds.
items.cn: dubitare 意为犹豫，与 duo（二）相关，画面是「心里分成两半」。

items.en: The noun dubium names a state of uncertainty, and dubius means doubtful.
items.cn: 名词 dubium 指不确定的状态，dubius 意为可疑的。

items.en: Douter carries the Romanic sense of hesitating between options.
items.cn: 古法语 douter 承接了「在两种可能之间犹豫」的含义。

items.en: Doubt settles into Middle English with the spelling of the French form.
items.cn: doubt 以法语拼写的形式进入中古英语。

items.en: The combination with un- gives undoubted, meaning free from doubt.
items.cn: 加 un- 后形成 undoubted，意为「没有疑问」。

items.en: Undoubted becomes especially common before abstract nouns such as talent, success, and authority.
items.cn: 现代英语中，undoubted 常修饰 talent、success、authority 等抽象名词。

note.en: Undoubted is the negative of doubt, and it stands beside words that mark a plain gap between belief and fact.
note.cn: undoubted 是否定形式的 doubt，与那些在信念和事实之间划清界限的词并列。

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
not sure, or unlikely
without question
known for sure
too clear to argue against
easy to see or understand

normalIntro.en: Undoubted is doubt with the door shut: un- removes the hesitation.
normalIntro.cn: undoubted 是关上一半的怀疑：un- 拿掉了那份犹豫。

normal.en: Doubt descends from Latin dubitare, to waver between two minds, so undoubted means no wavering.
normal.cn: doubt 源自拉丁语 dubitare（在两种心思之间摇摆），所以 undoubted 就是不再摇摆。

normal.en: The prefix un- is a clean negation, giving not doubted.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 是干脆的否定，构成「不被怀疑的」。

normal.en: Of undoubted quality is a common phrase for goods or work that everyone trusts.
normal.cn: of undoubted quality 常用来形容人人信得过的产品或工作。

normal.en: Compared with no doubt, undoubted is the adjective form used before nouns.
normal.cn: 与 no doubt 相比，undoubted 是修饰名词的形容词形式。

normal.en: Its adverb undoubtedly is far more common in IELTS writing than the adjective.
normal.cn: 它的副词 undoubtedly 在雅思写作中比形容词更常用。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed firmly onto a document, leaving no gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章稳稳压在文件上，不留缝隙。

abstract.en: Think of a scale that stops exactly at the mark with no wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤稳稳停在刻度上，一点也不晃。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd that falls silent because nothing needs asking.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人集体沉默，因为不需要再问什么。

examples.en: The scheme is of undoubted benefit to the town.
examples.cn: 这项计划对该镇无疑有好处。

examples.en: Her undoubted ability won her the scholarship.
examples.cn: 她无可置疑的能力为她赢得了奖学金。

examples.en: He remains the undoubted leader of the party.
examples.cn: 他仍是该党无可争议的领袖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺当剃的」——有人质疑就干脆「剃掉」，剃得一干二净，所以是「毫无疑问的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 否定前缀 un- + doubted（被怀疑的）；doubt 源自拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆、犹豫），一般认为与 duo（二）相关，画面「一心分作两半」，核心义「不再摇摆、无需核对」。

sensesIntro.en: Undoubted begins with a fact that needs no checking, widens to what everyone agrees on, and is finally used as a title for whoever clearly stands first.
sensesIntro.cn: undoubted 从一个无需核对的事实出发，扩展到众人一致认同的事，最后用作「明显第一者」的称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp pressed onto a document with no gap left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章严丝合缝地盖在文件上。

branches.en: A fact beyond doubt needs no second look.
branches.cn: 毫无疑问的事实无需再看第二眼。

branches.en: General agreement turns a strong claim into common ground.
branches.cn: 普遍认同把有力的断言变成了共识。

branches.en: Clear superiority becomes a plain title.
branches.cn: 明显的优势变成一个简单的称号。

branches.en: An undoubted star is simply someone whose merit nobody questions.
branches.cn: undoubted star 就是其价值无人质疑的那个人。

branches.en: Both senses rest on public consent rather than private proof.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都依赖公众共识而非私人证明。

intro.en: Undoubted is built from un-, doubt, and a participle ending, with derivatives such as undoubtedly and doubtless.
intro.cn: undoubted 由前缀 un-、词干 doubt 和分词词尾构成，派生词有 undoubtedly、doubtless 等。

latinIntro.en: Doubt goes back to Latin dubitare, to waver, which stands beside dubius, doubtful.
latinIntro.cn: doubt 上溯拉丁语 dubitare（摇摆），同族有 dubius（可疑的）。

items.example: The prefix un- gives undoubted its negative force.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 赋予 undoubted 否定的力量。

items.example: Doubt is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: doubt 是这一族词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms doubted and undoubted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 doubted 与 undoubted。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms doubtful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 doubtful。

items.example: The suffix -less forms doubtless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 doubtless。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms undoubtedly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 undoubtedly。

items.example: Undoubted is the whole unit.
items.exampleCN: undoubted 是完整的词形。

items.example: Undoubting shares the un- pattern.
items.exampleCN: undoubting 使用相同的 un- 构造。

items.example: A thing that nobody questions is undoubted.
items.exampleCN: 无人质疑的事物就是 undoubted。

definition_zh: 发掘；挖出；发现；揭露
definition_en: to dig up something buried in the ground, or to discover something that was hidden or unknown
core_image: 铁锹撬开泥土，把埋在地下的陶罐一点点露出来
scene: 考古队在遗址里小心地挖开泥土，让一只完整的陶罐重见天日。After months of careful digging, the team managed to unearth a complete clay pot.
sceneCN: 这里 unearth 是「挖出、发掘」（第 1 个义项：把埋在地下的东西取出来）；句意：经过几个月的仔细挖掘，队伍终于挖出了一只完整的陶罐。

pos.zh: 挖出；发掘；发现；揭露

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，指出土、发掘这一动作或其产物
基础名词，指泥土、地面，也是动词 unearth 的词根来源

senses.title: To dig something out of the ground
senses.definition: to remove something from the ground by digging
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从地里挖掘出来
senses.example: Farmers unearthed a stone tomb while ploughing the field.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在耕地时挖出了一座石墓。
senses.why: The prefix un- reverses a covering, so to unearth is to undo the earth that hides a thing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示撤销，泥土本来盖住东西，unearth 就是把覆盖的土去掉。

senses.title: To discover something hidden
senses.definition: to find or discover something that was hidden, lost, or forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 找到或发现原本隐藏、遗失或被遗忘的东西
senses.example: Researchers unearthed old maps in the museum archive.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在博物馆档案里发现了旧地图。
senses.why: Once the digging image is removed, the word extends to any search that turns up what was lying out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 去掉挖土的具体画面后，词义就扩展到任何翻找后让看不见的东西现身的过程。

senses.title: To bring a fact into the open
senses.definition: to reveal a fact, secret, or wrongdoing that others wanted to keep quiet
senses.definitionCN: 揭发他人想隐瞒的事实、秘密或过错
senses.example: The newspaper unearthed a fraud that had lasted for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸揭露了一桩持续多年的诈骗。
senses.why: What is buried in the ground and what is buried in silence feel the same, so the verb moves from soil to scandal.
senses.whyCN: 埋在地下的东西和瞒着不说的事在感觉上是一样的，所以这个词从泥土延伸到丑闻。

intro.en: Unearth is an English formation: the prefix un- meaning the reversal of an action, plus the noun earth.
intro.cn: unearth 是英语自身的构词：表示「撤销」的前缀 un- 加名词 earth（泥土）组成。

items.en: Eorþe is the native word for ground, soil, and the world.
items.cn: eorþe 是古英语中表示土地、泥土与世界的本族词。

items.en: The spelling settles as erthe or earth after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼征服之后，拼写逐渐固定为 erthe 或 earth。

items.en: The verb unearth appears, first used of lifting things out of the soil.
items.cn: 动词 unearth 出现，最初指把东西从土里取出来。

items.en: The sense widens to finding anything hidden or forgotten.
items.cn: 词义扩展到找到任何隐藏或被遗忘的东西。

items.en: Modern journalism and archaeology make it a standard word for revealing and excavating.
items.cn: 现代新闻与考古学使它成为表示「揭露」与「发掘」的常用词。

note.en: Group one holds words built on earth and the digging verb; group two holds other verbs of uncovering and finding.
note.cn: 第一组是以 earth 构成的词与挖掘动词；第二组是其他表示揭开与找到的动词。

entries.definition: The ground, soil, or the planet, which gives the second half of unearth.
entries.definitionCN: 地面、泥土或地球，构成本词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Made of baked clay or covered with soil.
The connection of an electric circuit to the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 电路接地，与土相关但意义不同。

entries.definition: To live in a place, from Latin habitare, unrelated to earth.
entries.definitionCN: 居住，来自拉丁语 habitare，与 earth 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To dig an area systematically, especially for scientific purposes.
entries.definitionCN: 系统挖掘，尤指科学发掘。

entries.definition: To remove something by digging, or to find old information.
entries.definitionCN: 挖出；也指翻找出旧信息。

entries.definition: To take a body out of a grave, much narrower than unearth.
entries.definitionCN: 掘出遗体，比 unearth 窄得多。

entries.definition: To make wrongdoing public, close to the revealing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使过错曝光，接近「揭露」义。

normalIntro.en: Unearth is literally to undo the earth: the prefix un- says take the soil away and let the thing show.
normalIntro.cn: unearth 字面上就是「解除泥土」：前缀 un- 表示把土去掉，让东西露出来。

normal.en: Un- plus earth: to remove the covering of soil.
normal.cn: un- 加 earth：去掉覆盖的泥土。

normal.en: Archaeologists unearth pottery and bones.
normal.cn: 考古学家发掘出陶器和骨骸。

normal.en: Reporters unearth scandals that others would hide.
normal.cn: 记者揭露别人想隐瞒的丑闻。

normal.en: Compare earth in earthenware, the same native root.
normal.cn: 对比 earthenware 里的 earth，是同一个本族词根。

normal.en: The past form unearthed is far more common than unearths in news writing.
normal.cn: 在新闻写作中，过去式 unearthed 比 unearths 常见得多。

abstract.en: Picture a spade lifting dark soil and a jar edge appearing.
abstract.cn: 想象铁锹铲起黑土，一只陶罐的边缘露出来。

abstract.en: Picture a dusty box pulled from the back of an archive shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象从档案架深处抽出一只满是灰尘的箱子。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope finally opened in front of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的信封终于当众拆开。

examples.en: Workers unearthed a Roman coin near the old bridge.
examples.cn: 工人们在旧桥附近挖出了一枚罗马硬币。

examples.en: The inquiry may unearth new evidence next week.
examples.cn: 调查下周可能会发掘出新证据。

examples.en: Old letters unearthed in the attic told a surprising story.
examples.cn: 在阁楼里翻出的旧信件讲出了一个令人意外的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安泥」——安心把泥挖开，东西才能重见天日；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本族构词：un-（撤销、去除）+ earth（古英语 eorþe，泥土、地面）→ unearth（把泥土去掉 → 挖出 → 发现 → 揭露），核心义「让被埋住的东西重见天日」。

sensesIntro.en: Unearth starts with lifting something out of the ground, then moves to finding hidden things, and finally to revealing what people tried to keep quiet.
sensesIntro.cn: unearth 先从土里挖出东西开始，再指找到隐藏之物，最后指揭发别人想瞒住的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade opening the soil until a buried jar shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锹撬开泥土，让埋着的陶罐露出来。

branches.en: Digging out a physical object is the original sense.
branches.cn: 挖出实物是最初的字面义。

branches.en: Finding something hidden is the search sense.
branches.cn: 找到隐藏之物是搜寻义。

branches.en: Revealing wrongdoing is the journalistic sense.
branches.cn: 揭发过错是新闻语域的义项。

branches.en: Both senses share the image of something lying out of sight beneath a surface.
branches.cn: 两个义项都有「藏在表层之下、看不见」的意象。

branches.en: A discovery becomes a revelation once it is made public.
branches.cn: 当发现被公之于众时，就变成了揭露。

intro.en: Unearth is a native English compound, so its parts are the prefix un- and the noun earth rather than a Latin root.
intro.cn: unearth 是英语本族复合词，构成成分是前缀 un- 与名词 earth，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is Germanic, but its relatives include Latin terms for ground and digging.
latinIntro.cn: 本词属于日耳曼语源，相关的拉丁词则多与「土地」和「挖掘」有关。

items.example: Un- in unearth removes the soil cover.
items.exampleCN: unearth 中的 un- 表示去掉泥土覆盖。

items.example: Earth is the object that un- undoes.
items.exampleCN: earth 正是 un- 要撤销的对象。

items.example: Unearth joins the two halves.
items.exampleCN: unearth 把两个部分合在一起。

items.example: Earthen pots survive burial well.
items.exampleCN: 陶罐在埋葬环境中能保存得很好。

items.example: Earthenware is what diggers often unearth.
items.exampleCN: 陶器是挖掘者经常出土的东西。

items.example: Earthing is an electrical term.
items.exampleCN: earthing 是电气术语。

items.example: Un- also negates as in unknown.
items.exampleCN: un- 也用于否定，如 unknown。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing gives unearthing.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ing 得到名词 unearthing。

definition_zh: 神秘的；非人间的；可怕的；离奇的；（时间）极早的
definition_en: strange and unpleasantly or eerily unnatural, as if not from this world, or unusually extreme in time
core_image: 深夜的天空裂开一道白光，照出不属于人间的奇异形状
scene: 山谷里传来一种从没听过的声音，像有人用不属于人间的嗓子在唱歌。From the valley rose an unearthly sound, as if something not human were singing.
sceneCN: 这里 unearthly 是「非人间的、怪异的」（第 1 个义项：不似人间所有、令人不安的怪异）；句意：山谷里传来一种非人间的声响，仿佛有什么不是人类的东西在唱歌。

pos.zh: 神秘的；非人间的；可怕的；离奇的；极早的

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 un- 的正向形式，义为「尘世的、人间的」
基础名词，指泥土与地球，是 earthliness 一族的根
earthly 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「尘世性、世俗性」

senses.title: Strange and not of this world
senses.definition: so strange or unnatural that it seems to come from another world
senses.definitionCN: 怪异或不自然得好像来自另一个世界
senses.example: A pale unearthly glow hung over the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 荒野上方悬着一片惨白奇异的光。
senses.why: Un- denies earthly status, so the adjective marks anything that seems to belong elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: un- 否定了 earth 的「人间」属性，所以这个词标记的是好像本来属于别处的东西。

senses.title: Frightening and ghostly
senses.definition: unnaturally frightening, like a ghost or a scream beyond human range
senses.definitionCN: 诡异得令人害怕，像鬼魂或超出人声范围的尖叫
senses.example: She let out an unearthly shriek in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黑暗中发出一声怪异的尖叫。
senses.why: The same denial of the human world shifts from wonder to dread when applied to sound and faces.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对人间的否定，用在声音与脸孔上时，感受就从惊奇转为恐惧。

senses.title: Extremely early or ill-timed
senses.definition: used of a time so early that it is almost beyond what a person normally does
senses.definitionCN: 形容时间早到几乎超出常人的作息
senses.example: We had to catch the train at an unearthly hour.
senses.exampleCN: 我们得在一个早得离谱的时刻去赶火车。
senses.why: An hour outside ordinary human hours is metaphorically outside the world people live in.
senses.whyCN: 落在常人行息之外的时刻，比喻上也就落在人所生活的世界之外。

intro.en: Unearthly is earth plus the adjective suffix -ly, with the negative prefix un- in front.
intro.cn: unearthly 由名词 earth 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，前面再加否定前缀 un-。

items.en: Eorþlic means belonging to the earth or this world.
items.cn: eorþlic 意为属于大地或此世的。

items.en: Earthly keeps that sense of what concerns mortal life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 earthly 保留「关乎此生」这一含义。

items.en: Unearthly appears, used of sights and sounds unlike anything in nature.
items.cn: unearthly 出现，用于形容与自然之物不同的景象与声音。

items.en: Gothic fiction and poetry make it a favourite word for ghosts and gloom.
items.cn: 哥特小说与诗歌使它成为描写鬼魅与阴森的常用词。

items.en: The fixed phrase an unearthly hour becomes the everyday idiom.
items.cn: 固定搭配「早得离谱的时刻」成为日常习语。

note.en: Group one holds words built on earth; group two holds adjectives for what seems not human.
note.cn: 第一组是以 earth 构成的词；第二组是表示「不属于人间」的形容词。

entries.definition: Connected with life on earth, with no prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 尘世的、人间的，没有前缀。

entries.definition: Unable to leave the ground or tied to practical matters.
entries.definitionCN: 离不开地面的；拘泥于现实的。

entries.definition: Not real, or so odd that it hardly seems possible, sharing the same shadow of doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实的，或怪异得几乎不像真的，与本词共享同一种可疑感。

entries.definition: Belonging to a realm beyond nature, a cooler and more formal term.
Like a ghost, pale and faint.
Dreadful or excessive, often used of noise at odd hours.
entries.definitionCN: 可怕的、过分的，常形容怪时间的声响。

entries.definition: Belonging to or suggesting another world, often in a calm way.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个世界的，语气常更平和。

normalIntro.en: Unearthly is un plus earthly: not of this earth, so strange that it seems to come from somewhere else.
normalIntro.cn: unearthly 是 un 加 earthly：不属此世，所以显得好像来自别处。

normal.en: Earthly means of this world, and un- turns it inside out.
normal.cn: earthly 意为此世的，un- 把它翻转过来。

normal.en: An unearthly light in the sky terrifies the villagers.
normal.cn: 天上的奇异光亮让村民们惊恐。

normal.en: An unearthly hour is far too early, as in before dawn.
normal.cn: unearthly hour 指早得离谱的时刻，例如天亮之前。

normal.en: Compare earthly and unearthly: the prefix decides whether it belongs here.
normal.cn: 对比 earthly 与 unearthly：前缀决定它属不属于此世。

normal.en: The word suits horror films that want an eerie glow or scream.
normal.cn: 这个词适合需要诡异光亮或尖叫的恐怖片场景。

abstract.en: Picture moonlight on a lake that glows greener than any lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象月光照在湖面上，光绿得比任何灯都奇怪。

abstract.en: Picture a voice singing a note no human throat could reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一个嗓音唱出人的喉咙达不到的音。

abstract.en: Picture an alarm clock ringing while the sky is still black.
abstract.cn: 想象天还全黑时闹钟就响了。

examples.en: An unearthly silence fell over the empty stadium.
examples.cn: 空荡的体育场里落下一片诡异的寂静。

examples.en: The mushrooms gave off an unearthly blue light.
examples.cn: 那些蘑菇发出奇异的蓝光。

examples.en: She rang me at an unearthly hour to share the news.
examples.cn: 她在天还没亮的时候打电话告诉我这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不思理」——遇到非人间的怪事，人一时想不通其中的道理；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本族构词：un-（否定）+ earth（古英语 eorþe，大地、人间）+ -ly（形容词后缀）→ unearthly（不属人间的 → 奇异的 → 可怕的 → 早得离谱的），核心义「不属于此世」。

sensesIntro.en: Unearthly begins with denying that something belongs to the human world, turns that into dread, and ends as a fixed idiom about absurdly early hours.
sensesIntro.cn: unearthly 先否认某物属于人间，再由此转为恐惧，最后成为形容时间早得离谱的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glow that does not belong to the sky of this world.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道不属于此世天空的光。

branches.en: The first sense is the bare negation of earthly.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是 earthly 的直接否定。

branches.en: Fear is the emotional colour the negation takes in stories.
branches.cn: 恐惧是这种否定在故事中染上的情绪色彩。

branches.en: The time idiom reads an hour outside the human day.
branches.cn: 时间义把「超出常人行息的一天」读成比喻。

branches.en: Wonder passes into dread through the same image of the not-human.
branches.cn: 惊奇到恐惧的转变靠的是同一幅「非人」画面。

branches.en: Both the glow and the hour lie beyond ordinary human experience.
branches.cn: 奇异的光与离谱的时刻都超出常人的经验范围。

intro.en: Unearthly hides a whole word family: un-, earth, -ly, and the contrasting adjective earthly.
intro.cn: unearthly 背后是一整族词：un-、earth、-ly，以及对照的形容词 earthly。

latinIntro.en: The family is Germanic, but Latin has exact counterparts for earth and for the negating prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族属日耳曼语源，但拉丁语在「土地」和否定前缀上都有对应形式。

items.example: Un- makes earthly into unearthly.
items.exampleCN: un- 把 earthly 变成 unearthly。

items.example: Earth names the human world here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 earth 指人间世界。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly builds earthly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 earthly。

items.example: Earthly pleasures pass quickly.
items.exampleCN: 尘世的快乐很快消逝。

items.example: Unearthly sounds fill the story.
items.exampleCN: 非人间的声响充满这篇故事。

items.meaning: possible, as in no earthly reason
items.meaningCN: 可能的，如毫无可能的理由
items.example: Earthly also means possible at all.
items.exampleCN: earthly 还可以表示「到底、根本」。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness builds earthliness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 earthliness。

items.example: Earthliness contrasts with the unearthly.
items.exampleCN: earthliness 与非人间的相对。

definition_zh: 不平的；不均匀的；不均衡的；忽高忽低的；质量不一的；奇数的
definition_en: not level or not equal: bumpy in surface, unequal in amount, irregular in rhythm, or not matching in standard
core_image: 一张瘸了腿的桌子：桌面一边高一边低，桌上的杯子全都在滑动
scene: 木板路有几块坏了，走在上面深一脚浅一脚，还差点被绊倒。The wooden path was uneven, so we stumbled where the boards had lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 uneven 是「不平整的」（第 1 个义项：表面高低不平、有凸起）；句意：这条木板路凹凸不平，我们走到翘起的板子那里就打趔趄。

pos.zh: 不平的；不均匀的；不均衡的；质量不一的；奇数的

derivatives.zh: uneven 加 -ly 构成，义为「不均匀地、不平地」
uneven 加 -ness 构成，义为「不平整；不均衡」
去掉前缀 un- 的正向形式，义为「平坦的；相等的；偶数的」

senses.title: Not level or flat
senses.definition: not smooth or level, so that things on it topple or feet stumble
senses.definitionCN: 表面不平或不水平，上面的东西会倾斜，走路会绊
senses.example: Cyclists fell on the uneven road.
senses.exampleCN: 骑车的人在不平的路面上摔倒。
senses.why: Un- simply removes even, whose oldest sense is flat and level.
senses.whyCN: un- 直接取消 even 的含义，而 even 最早的意思就是平坦、水平。

senses.title: Not equal in amount
senses.definition: different in size, number, or amount where one would expect a balance
senses.definitionCN: 在应当均衡的地方，在大小、数量或份额上相差明显
senses.example: Rainfall is very uneven across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区的降雨很不均匀。
senses.why: The second old sense of even is equal, so an uneven share is one that has broken a balance.
senses.whyCN: even 的第二个古老含义是相等，所以「不均衡的分配」就是打破了平衡的分配。

senses.title: Not steady in pace or quality
senses.titleCN: 忽快忽慢的；质量不一的
senses.definition: changing from one moment to another in speed, effort, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 在速度、用力或水平上时好时坏、不稳定
senses.example: The students made uneven progress during the term.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们这学期进步很不稳定。
senses.why: A level, even line is the image of constancy, so a break in the line becomes a break in performance.
senses.whyCN: 平直的线是「稳定」的画面，线一断，稳定也跟着断，于是就有了表现上的起伏。

senses.title: Not divisible by two
senses.definition: used of a whole number that cannot be divided equally by two
senses.definitionCN: 指不能被二整除的整数
senses.example: Groups with an uneven total cannot split into fair teams.
senses.exampleCN: 人数是奇数的组无法分成公平的两队。
senses.why: Even has long meant paired, so uneven numbers are those that will not pair up.
senses.whyCN: even 一直有「成双」的意思，奇数就是配不成对的那一类数。

intro.en: Uneven rests on the Old English adjective efen, meaning level, equal, and paired, with the prefix un- added.
intro.cn: uneven 建立在古英语形容词 efen 之上，意为平坦、相等、成对，再加否定前缀 un-。

items.en: Efen describes what is level, equal, or in pairs.
items.cn: efen 形容平坦、相等或成对的东西。

items.en: The spelling shifts towards even while the old senses survive.
items.cn: 拼写转向 even，而原有的几个含义都保留下来。

items.en: Uneven records surfaces that are not level.
items.cn: uneven 记载的是「不平整」的表面。

items.en: The word is extended to unequal shares and to uneven numbers.
items.cn: 词义扩展到分配不均与奇数。

items.en: Modern usage adds uneven performance and rather uneven contests.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了形容表现不稳与实力悬殊的说法。

note.en: Group one holds the even family; group two holds other words for unequal surfaces and shares.
note.cn: 第一组是 even 词族；第二组是其他表示表面不平或份额不等的词。

entries.definition: Flat, equal, or divisible by two, the positive of uneven.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的、相等的或偶数的，是 uneven 的正向形式。

entries.definition: In a flat or equal way, the opposite of unevenly.
entries.definitionCN: 均匀地、平平地，与 unevenly 相对。

entries.definition: With nothing interesting happening, from event, only close in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无事的，来自 event，与本词只是拼写开头相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: Not smooth to the touch, often about texture.
Full of bumps, used of roads and rides.
entries.definitionCN: 满是凸起，多形容路面与颠簸。

entries.definition: Not following a fixed shape or pattern in time or space.
With one side heavier or larger than the other.
entries.definitionCN: 一边重或大、偏向一侧的。

normalIntro.en: Uneven is even with a negative prefix, so think of a line that has lost its level.
normalIntro.cn: uneven 是 even 加了否定前缀，可以想成一条失去水平的线。

normal.en: Even means level and equal, so un- takes both away at once.
normal.cn: even 兼有平坦与相等两义，un- 一下子把两者都取消。

normal.en: Uneven ground is the first thing a hiker notices.
normal.cn: 徒步的人最先注意到的就是不平的地面。

normal.en: An uneven distribution of water is a classic geography topic.
normal.cn: 水资源分布不均是很典型的地理话题。

normal.en: Even numbers pair up while uneven numbers are left over.
normal.cn: 偶数能两两配对，奇数会剩下。

normal.en: The adverbs unevenly and evenly swap meaning with one prefix.
normal.cn: 副词 unevenly 与 evenly 只差一个前缀，意思正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a table rocking on one short leg.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子因一条腿短而晃来晃去。

abstract.en: Picture one tall glass of water and one short one on the same table.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张桌上放着一高杯水和一矮杯水。

abstract.en: Picture a runner whose speed keeps jumping up and down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者速度忽快忽慢。

examples.en: The old floor is uneven and creaks in the middle.
examples.cn: 旧地板不平，中间还吱吱作响。

examples.en: Growth has been uneven between cities and villages.
examples.cn: 城乡之间的发展并不均衡。

examples.en: His grades are uneven, good in maths but weak in writing.
examples.cn: 他的成绩很不均衡，数学好而写作弱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不平」——俺走的这条路根本不平；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本族构词：un-（否定）+ 古英语 efen / 中古英语 even（平坦的；相等的；成对的）→ uneven（不平的 → 不均衡的 → 不稳定的 → 奇数的），核心义「失去了水平与对等」。

sensesIntro.en: Uneven begins with the loss of a flat surface, moves to unequal shares and unsteady quality, and ends with numbers that will not pair.
sensesIntro.cn: uneven 从失去平坦表面开始，转到份额不等与表现不稳，最后指配不成对的奇数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table rocking on one short leg.
core.cn: 核心意象：缺了一条腿的桌子摇晃不平。

branches.en: A surface that is not flat is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 表面不平是这一族词的身体经验义。

branches.en: Unequal shares extend levelness to quantity.
branches.cn: 不均的份额把「平」的概念扩展到数量。

branches.en: Unsteady quality extends it to performance over time.
branches.cn: 不稳的表现把「平」的概念扩展到时间上的表现。

branches.en: A broken balance underlies both a bumpy road and an unfair share.
branches.cn: 颠簸的路面与不公平的分配背后都是平衡被打破。

branches.en: Odd numbers are the countable version of things that will not pair.
branches.cn: 奇数是「配不成对」在数字上的说法。

intro.en: Uneven is a native English pair: the prefix un- and the very old adjective even, plus its two suffixes.
intro.cn: uneven 是英语本族的一对：前缀 un- 与古老的形容词 even，外加它的两个后缀。

latinIntro.en: The pair is Germanic, but Latin has words for level ground and for the equality even carries.
latinIntro.cn: 这一对属于日耳曼语源，不过拉丁语在「平地」与「相等」上也都有对应词。

items.example: Un- makes even into uneven.
items.exampleCN: un- 把 even 变成 uneven。

items.example: Even ground makes walking easy.
items.exampleCN: 平坦的地面走起来轻松。

items.example: Uneven steps are dangerous.
items.exampleCN: 台阶不平很危险。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds unevenly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 unevenly。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness builds unevenness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 unevenness。

items.example: Even numbers pair up neatly.
items.exampleCN: 偶数能整齐配对。

items.meaning: not the same in size or worth
items.example: Unequal pay is unfair.
items.exampleCN: 同工不同酬是不公平的。

items.example: Evenness of tone matters in speech.
items.exampleCN: 语调平稳在说话中很重要。

definition_zh: 不熟悉的；陌生的；不常见的；生疏的
definition_en: not known or not experienced before; not having knowledge of something
core_image: 推开一扇门，门后是完全没见过的房间
scene: 搬到新城市的第一晚，他站在陌生的街道上找不到回家的路。On his first night in a new city, he stood on an unfamiliar street and could not find his way home.
sceneCN: 这里 unfamiliar 是「陌生的」（第 1 个义项：此前没见过、不了解的事物）；句意：搬到新城市的第一晚，他站在陌生的街道上找不到回家的路。

pos.zh: 不熟悉的；陌生的
对……不熟悉的；生疏的

collocations.zh: 陌生的领域；未知的处境

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀 un- 后的基础词，义为「熟悉的」
unfamiliar 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「陌生、不熟悉」
familiar 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「熟悉、亲密」
familiar 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使熟悉」

senses.title: Not known before
senses.definition: never seen, heard, or experienced before, and therefore strange
senses.definitionCN: 以前没见过、没听过或没经历过的，因而显得奇怪
senses.example: The night sky looked completely unfamiliar to her.
senses.exampleCN: 那片夜空在她看来完全陌生。
senses.why: The prefix un- simply turns familiar into its opposite, so the word names things the mind cannot yet place.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 只是把 familiar 翻转成反义，词义指向头脑还无法归位的事物。

senses.title: Not knowledgeable about
senses.definition: having little or no knowledge or experience of something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事了解很少或没有经验
senses.example: Many drivers are unfamiliar with the new traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 许多司机对新交通规则不熟悉。
senses.why: When the word takes with or to, the absence of familiarity is placed in a person and points to a gap in knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 当它搭配 with 或 to 时，陌生的状态被放进某个人身上，指向知识上的空缺。

senses.title: Rare or not commonly encountered
senses.definition: not often met, used, or found in ordinary circumstances
senses.definitionCN: 在日常情形中很少遇到、使用或发现的
senses.example: The recipe uses a spice unfamiliar in this region.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜用了一种在本地区不常见的香料。
senses.why: What is unfamiliar is by definition outside everyday routine, so the word can describe rarity rather than strangeness.
senses.whyCN: 陌生的东西本就在日常习惯之外，因此这个词也能描述稀少，而不只是奇怪。

senses.title: A person who is a stranger
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe a person or face that is not recognized
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，描述不被认出来的人或面孔
senses.example: The quiet town was full of unfamiliar faces that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天，这个安静的小镇上到处都是陌生的面孔。
senses.why: The same sense of not being placed is applied to people, so a newcomer becomes an unfamiliar face.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「无法归位」之感用在人身上，外来者就成了陌生的面孔。

senses.title: Lacking skill through disuse
senses.definition: no longer skilled at something because one has not done it for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 因为长时间没做某事而技巧变得生疏
senses.example: My typing feels unfamiliar after weeks without practice.
senses.exampleCN: 几周没练习后，我打字都感到生疏。
senses.why: Familiarity is built by repeated contact, so when contact stops the easy flow of a skill becomes unfamiliar again.
senses.whyCN: 熟悉靠反复接触建立，接触一旦中断，熟练的流畅感又变得陌生。

senses.title: Unpleasantly strange
senses.titleCN: 古怪的；令人不自在的陌生
senses.definition: giving a feeling of unease because it is not like what one normally knows
senses.definitionCN: 因为与通常所知不同而让人感到不安
senses.example: There was an unfamiliar smell in the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 空房子里有一股陌生的气味。
senses.why: The strange and the unnoticed coincide here: what is not recognized creates a mild sense of unease.
senses.whyCN: 陌生与未被识别在此重合：认不出来的东西会带来轻微的不安。

intro.en: Unfamiliar is the Latin adjective familiar joined to the English negative prefix un-, meaning not.
intro.cn: unfamiliar 由拉丁语形容词 familiar 加上英语否定前缀 un-（表示「不」）构成。

items.en: Familia means a household and the people and slaves within it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 familia 指家庭以及家中的成员。

items.en: Familiaris means belonging to a household, and therefore close or intimate.
items.cn: familiaris 意为属于家庭的，引申为亲近、亲密的。

items.en: Familier carries the adjective closer to the modern sense of well known.
items.cn: 古法语 familier 把这一形容词带向「熟知的」现代义。

items.en: Familiar enters English meaning closely associated with or well known.
items.cn: familiar 进入英语，意为关系密切或为人熟知。

items.en: Old English un- becomes a live negative prefix attached to adjectives such as familiar.
items.cn: 古英语的 un- 成为能产的否定前缀，加在 familiar 这类形容词前。

items.en: Unfamiliar settles into the senses of strange, unknown, and not experienced.
items.cn: unfamiliar 最终固定为「陌生的、未知的、缺乏经验的」等义。

note.en: Unfamiliar belongs to the family of familiar words and is close in meaning to strange and unknown.
note.cn: unfamiliar 属于 familiar 这一词族，在意思上接近 strange 与 unknown。

entries.definition: well known or easily recognized
the state of being unknown or strange
to make someone used to something
unusual or surprising in a way that is hard to explain
not identified or not yet known
belonging to a place or group that is not one s own

normalIntro.en: Unfamiliar is simply familiar wearing the negative cloak of un-, so it marks what has not yet joined the household of the mind.
normalIntro.cn: unfamiliar 就是披上否定外衣的 familiar，标记出尚未进入头脑这个「家」的东西。

normal.en: The prefix un- negates, and familiar comes from Latin familia, a household.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 表否定，familiar 来自拉丁语 familia（家庭）。

normal.en: Something familiar once belonged to the household of your knowledge.
normal.cn: 熟悉的东西，曾经属于你知识里的「家」。

normal.en: Unfamiliar with is the standard phrase for lacking knowledge of a subject.
normal.cn: unfamiliar with 是表示「对某主题缺乏了解」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Unfamiliar to means that a thing is new to the people concerned.
normal.cn: unfamiliar to 表示某事物对相关的人来说是新的。

normal.en: Compare strange: strange often suggests oddness, unfamiliar mainly suggests what is not known.
normal.cn: 对比 strange：strange 常暗示古怪，unfamiliar 主要指「不认识」。

abstract.en: Picture a map with large blank patches where no landmark is drawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，大片空白处没有任何地标。

abstract.en: Imagine typing a shortcut that your hands have never learned.
abstract.cn: 想象你敲一个手从未学会的快捷键。

abstract.en: Think of the smell of a house you have never entered before.
abstract.cn: 想想一间你从未进过的房子里的气味。

examples.en: The town felt unfamiliar to the new teacher.
examples.cn: 这个小镇让新来的老师感到陌生。

examples.en: She was unfamiliar with the software and asked for help.
examples.cn: 她不熟悉这款软件，于是请求帮助。

examples.en: Unfamiliar faces filled the lecture hall.
examples.cn: 阶梯教室里坐满了陌生的面孔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺 fami 里」——连「俺家里」都认不清了，当然是陌生的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语否定前缀 un-（不）+ 拉丁语 familia（家庭）→ familiaris（家里的；亲近的）→ familiar（熟悉的）→ unfamiliar（不熟悉的；陌生的），核心义「尚未进入「家」这个熟悉圈」。

sensesIntro.en: Unfamiliar starts from what is not yet known, then moves to a person who lacks knowledge of something, and finally to rarity, strangers, rusty skills, and mild unease.
sensesIntro.cn: unfamiliar 从「尚不认识的事物」出发，过渡到「某人对某事缺乏了解」，再延伸到稀少、陌生人、生疏的技巧与轻微的不安。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door opening on a room never entered before.
core.cn: 核心意象：推开一扇门，门后是完全没见过的房间。

branches.en: A thing not yet seen is the basic sense of strangeness.
branches.cn: 尚未见过的事物构成最基本的「陌生」义。

branches.en: A person with little knowledge of a subject is the with and to sense.
branches.cn: 对某主题缺乏了解的人，就是搭配 with 与 to 时的义项。

branches.en: Rarity follows because what lies outside routine is seldom met.
branches.cn: 稀少义随之而来，因为日常之外的事物很少遇到。

branches.en: Applied to people, the same absence of recognition makes a stranger.
branches.cn: 用在人身上时，同样的「认不出」便造就了陌生人。

branches.en: A skill made unfamiliar by disuse and a strange smell both disturb the ease of habit.
branches.cn: 因荒废而变生的技巧和陌生的气味，都打破了习惯的安稳。

intro.en: Unfamiliar is built from the negative prefix un- and the Latin root familia, with a whole family of familiar words around it.
intro.cn: unfamiliar 由否定前缀 un- 与拉丁词根 familia 构成，周围还有一整族 familiar 相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia means a household, and familiaris means belonging to it, hence intimate or well known.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 familia 意为家庭，familiaris 意为属于家庭的，因此引申为亲近、熟知。

items.example: The prefix un- negates familiar.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 给 familiar 加上了否定。

items.example: Familia gives the core idea of a household.
items.exampleCN: familia 提供了「家户」这一核心概念。

items.example: Familiaris is the direct source of familiar.
items.exampleCN: familiaris 是 familiar 的直接来源。

items.example: Familiar is the base word.
items.exampleCN: familiar 是基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity forms unfamiliarity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 unfamiliarity。

items.meaning: the state of being strange or unknown
items.example: Unfamiliarity names the abstract state.
items.exampleCN: unfamiliarity 指这种抽象状态。

items.meaningCN: 表示「使变成」的动词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ize forms familiarize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 familiarize。

items.meaning: to make someone familiar with something
items.example: Familiarize turns the state into an action.
items.exampleCN: familiarize 把状态变成了动作。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb unfamiliarly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 unfamiliarly。

definition_zh: 从容的；不慌不忙的；慢条斯理的
definition_en: moving or acting in a relaxed way, without hurry or pressure
core_image: 一个人端着一杯热茶，慢慢走过午后的长街
scene: 午后的咖啡馆里，老人不慌不忙地翻着报纸，等雨停。In the afternoon cafe, an old man turned the pages of his newspaper in an unhurried way, waiting for the rain to stop.
sceneCN: 这里 unhurried 是「不慌不忙的」（第 1 个义项：没有匆忙与压力，动作从容）；句意：午后的咖啡馆里，老人不慌不忙地翻着报纸，等雨停。

pos.zh: 不慌不忙的；从容的
常用 unhurriedly 形式，义为「从容地」

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀 un- 后的基础词，义为「匆忙的」
unhurried 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「从容地」
动词原形，义为「赶快、催促」
hurried 加 -ly 构成，义为「匆忙地」

senses.title: Moving without haste
senses.definition: moving at a relaxed speed, without any sense of rushing
senses.definitionCN: 以放松的速度移动，没有任何匆忙感
senses.example: An unhurried walk along the river cleared her mind.
senses.exampleCN: 沿河不慌不忙地散步，让她头脑清醒。
senses.why: The prefix un- negates hurried, so the word literally means not rushed, and speed becomes a matter of ease.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 否定 hurried，字面就是「不匆忙」，于是速度变成了一种从容的状态。

senses.title: Calm in manner
senses.definition: speaking or acting in a calm way that cannot be rushed
senses.definitionCN: 说话或做事平静，不会被催促打乱
senses.example: Her unhurried voice soothed the nervous child.
senses.exampleCN: 她从容的声音安抚了紧张的孩子。
senses.why: Once speed is removed, the remaining quality is calmness of manner, a steady inner pace.
senses.whyCN: 速度因素被抽掉之后，剩下的就是举止的沉稳，是内心稳定的节奏。

senses.title: Leisurely and comfortable
senses.definition: offering a comfortable, pleasurable pace with no pressure of time
senses.definitionCN: 提供舒适愉快的节奏，没有时间压力
senses.example: The village has an unhurried charm that tourists love.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄有一种游客喜爱的悠闲魅力。
senses.why: The absence of hurry is not merely neutral but pleasant, so the word can praise a place or a mood.
senses.whyCN: 没有匆忙不只是中性状态，还是愉快的，所以这个词能用来赞美一个地方或一种心境。

senses.title: Detailed and careful
senses.definition: done with enough time to be careful and thorough
senses.definitionCN: 有足够时间做得仔细而周全
senses.example: The committee took an unhurried look at every proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不慌不忙地逐一审阅了每份提案。
senses.why: Slowness allows attention, so not rushing naturally shades into care and thoroughness.
senses.whyCN: 慢下来才能留意，所以「不赶」自然引申出细心与周全。

senses.title: Steady rather than slowing down
senses.definition: keeping a constant, even pace without pauses or sudden changes
senses.definitionCN: 保持恒定均匀的节奏，没有停顿或突然变化
senses.example: The music kept an unhurried rhythm for the whole piece.
senses.exampleCN: 整首曲子始终保持着均匀的节奏。
senses.why: An unbroken pace without jerks is one way of being unhurried, applied to movement and rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 没有急停急起的均匀节奏，也是「不慌不忙」的一种体现，用于动作与节奏。

senses.title: A person with a slow temperament
senses.definition: describing a person who naturally works at a slow, easy tempo
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个天生节奏缓慢、轻松的人
senses.example: He is an unhurried man who never seems to worry.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个性子慢的人，似乎从不着急。
senses.why: The adjective applied to a person turns a temporary pace into a settled trait of character.
senses.whyCN: 用在人身上时，临时的节奏就固定成了性格特质。

intro.en: Unhurried is formed in English from the negative prefix un- and the adjective hurried, itself built on the verb hurry.
intro.cn: unhurried 是在英语内部由否定前缀 un- 加形容词 hurried 构成的，而 hurried 又来自动词 hurry。

items.en: A reconstructed root describing movement in a hurry is thought to be the distant source, though this is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为可追溯到某个描述匆忙动作的日耳曼语重构词根，但这一点并不确定。

items.en: The verb hurry appears in English, with the idea of driving someone along or bustling about.
items.cn: 动词 hurry 出现在英语中，带有推着人赶路、忙乱奔走的意味。

items.en: The past participle hurried develops into an adjective meaning rushed or done too fast.
items.cn: 过去分词 hurried 发展出形容词用法，意为仓促的、做得太快的。

items.en: The negative un- joins hurried, giving a settled adjective for calm, easy movement.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 加到 hurried 前，形成表示从容、轻松动作的固定形容词。

items.en: Unhurried spreads from movement to manner, mood, and rhythm in modern descriptions.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，unhurried 从动作扩展到举止、心境与节奏。

note.en: Unhurried sits in the family of hurry words and is close in meaning to relaxed and leisurely.
note.cn: unhurried 属于 hurry 这一词族，在意思上接近 relaxed 与 leisurely。

entries.definition: done quickly, sometimes too quickly
in a calm and relaxed way
to move or do something quickly
calm and not worried about small things
done without hurrying, often for pleasure
moving at a low speed

normalIntro.en: Unhurried is hurried with the hurry taken out, so the word carries the same root as a calm walk, not a rushed one.
normalIntro.cn: unhurried 就是把 hurried 里的「急」抽掉，所以它和 hurried 同根，却指向从容而非匆忙的脚步。

normal.en: The prefix un- negates the adjective hurried.
normal.cn: 前缀 un- 否定形容词 hurried。

normal.en: Hurry first appears in English as a verb about bustling along.
normal.cn: hurry 最早在英语中作动词出现，表示忙乱奔走。

normal.en: The phrase in an unhurried way is the most common adverbial use.
normal.cn: in an unhurried way 是最常见的副词性用法。

normal.en: An unhurried pace is the standard pairing for speed of movement.
normal.cn: unhurried pace 是描述移动速度的标准搭配。

normal.en: Compare leisurely: leisurely stresses enjoyment, unhurried stresses the absence of pressure.
normal.cn: 对比 leisurely：leisurely 强调享受，unhurried 强调没有压力。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking with a full cup of tea and not spilling a drop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人端着一杯满满的茶走着，一滴也没洒。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock ticking a little more slowly than the day requires.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的滴答比这一天的节奏稍慢一点。

abstract.en: Think of a wide river that keeps the same quiet speed all afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽阔的河，整个下午都保持同样安静的流速。

examples.en: They strolled through the market in an unhurried way.
examples.cn: 他们不慌不忙地逛着市场。

examples.en: The service was friendly and unhurried.
examples.cn: 服务既友善又从容。

examples.en: An unhurried morning gave her time to think.
examples.cn: 一个悠闲的早晨给了她思考的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安喝瑞的」——安心地喝茶，不急着走，就是从容不迫；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语否定前缀 un-（不）+ 动词 hurry（赶快）→ 过去分词 hurried（匆忙的）+ un- → unhurried（不慌不忙的），核心义「把匆忙去掉」。

sensesIntro.en: Unhurried begins with the plain absence of speed and extends to calm manner, pleasant leisure, careful work, even rhythm, and a slow temperament.
sensesIntro.cn: unhurried 从「纯粹没有速度压力」出发，延伸到沉稳的举止、悠闲的慢节奏、细致的工作、均匀的节奏以及慢条斯理的性情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person carrying hot tea who never spills a drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人端着热茶，慢慢走过午后的长街，一滴也不洒。

branches.en: Simply not rushing is the physical sense of unhurried movement.
branches.cn: 单纯地不急，就是 unhurried 的身体动作义。

branches.en: A calm voice shows the manner sense of steady composure.
branches.cn: 从容的声音体现的是举止沉稳的义项。

branches.en: Leisure and pleasure grow from a pace free of time pressure.
branches.cn: 悠闲与愉悦生长于没有时间压力的节奏之中。

branches.en: Careful review and even rhythm both come from a pace that does not jump or stop.
branches.cn: 细致的审阅与均匀的节奏，都来自不急停急起的步调。

branches.en: Applied to a person, the pace settles into a temperament.
branches.cn: 用在人身上，这种节奏便沉淀为性情。

intro.en: Unhurried pairs the negative prefix un- with the hurry word family, so the affix removes haste rather than adding it.
intro.cn: unhurried 把否定前缀 un- 与 hurry 词族配对，前缀在这里是「去掉」匆忙，而不是增添。

latinIntro.en: Unhurried has no Latin ancestry: hurry is of uncertain Germanic origin, so the Latin entries here are empty.
latinIntro.cn: unhurried 没有拉丁语渊源：hurry 的来源一般认为与日耳曼语有关但存疑，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix un- negates hurried.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定 hurried。

items.example: Hurry is the root verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: hurry 是这个词族的根动词。

items.example: The noun hurry names the pressure of time.
items.exampleCN: 名词 hurry 指时间带来的压力。

items.meaning: forming an adjective from a verb
items.meaningCN: 把动词变成形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms hurried.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 hurried。

items.example: Hurried is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: hurried 是基础形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unhurriedly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 unhurriedly。

items.example: Unhurriedly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: unhurriedly 把形容词变成了副词。

items.example: Hurriedly is the exact opposite adverb.
items.exampleCN: hurriedly 是意思完全相反的副词。

items.example: Over-hurried adds a prefix of excess.
items.exampleCN: over-hurried 加了表示过度的前缀。

definition_zh: 难以想象的；不可想象的；难以置信的
definition_en: so strange, large, or terrible that it is difficult or impossible to imagine
core_image: 脑海中画到一半就空白了的画布
scene: 洪水退去，整条街只剩泥浆，这种破坏在当地难以想象。When the flood withdrew, the whole street was left in mud, and such damage was unimaginable to local people.
sceneCN: 这里 unimaginable 是「难以想象的」（第 1 个义项：大到无法在脑中描绘）；句意：洪水退去，整条街只剩泥浆，这种破坏在当地难以想象。

pos.zh: 难以想象的；不可想象的
难以置信的；糟糕得难以想象的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀 un- 后的基础词，义为「可想象的」
动词原形，义为「想象」
加 -ation 构成，义为「想象力」
加 -ive 构成，义为「富有想象力的」
unimaginable 加 -ly 构成，义为「难以想象地」

senses.title: Too great to imagine
senses.definition: so large, huge, or extreme that the mind cannot picture it
senses.definitionCN: 规模或程度大到头脑无法描绘
senses.example: The universe contains unimaginable numbers of stars.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙中有着数量难以想象的恒星。
senses.why: The suffix -able says a thing can be done, and un- denies it, so unimaginable marks what lies beyond the reach of imagination.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 表示「可以」，un- 将其否定，所以 unimaginable 标记想象力够不到的东西。

senses.title: Hard to believe
senses.definition: so surprising that people find it difficult to accept as true
senses.definitionCN: 太过意外，人们很难相信它是真的
senses.example: It is unimaginable that he left without saying goodbye.
senses.exampleCN: 他一声不响就离开了，这简直难以想象。
senses.why: If the mind cannot build the picture, belief is hard to reach too, so the word comes to signal disbelief.
senses.whyCN: 头脑画不出这个画面，信念也就难以抵达，于是这个词表示「不敢相信」。

senses.title: Deeply distressing
senses.definition: so painful or terrible that one would never wish or expect it
senses.definitionCN: 痛苦或糟糕到人们从不愿想象也不曾预料
senses.example: Refugees told of unimaginable suffering in the camps.
senses.exampleCN: 难民们讲述了难民营里难以想象的苦难。
senses.why: The word often frames suffering that no ordinary mind can hold, giving it a strong emotional charge.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常用来描述超出常人心智承受的苦难，因此带有强烈的情感色彩。

senses.title: Not yet conceived
senses.titleCN: 尚未想到的；前所未有的
senses.definition: not yet thought of or invented by anyone
senses.definitionCN: 还没有人想到或发明过
senses.example: The phone brought unimaginable ways to talk to friends.
senses.exampleCN: 手机带来了从前难以想象的聊天方式。
senses.why: What has never entered imagination has never been conceived, so the word can describe brand new possibilities.
senses.whyCN: 从未进入想象的，也就从未被构想出来，因此这个词可以描述全新的可能。

senses.title: Beyond ordinary experience
senses.definition: outside the range of what most people have ever seen or felt
senses.definitionCN: 超出大多数人见过或感受过的范围
senses.example: For the villagers, clean water was unimaginable before the well was dug.
senses.exampleCN: 在挖井之前，干净的水对村民来说是难以想象的。
senses.why: The line between imaginable and unimaginable is drawn by experience, so the word often marks a boundary of daily life.
senses.whyCN: 可想象与不可思议之间的界线由经验划出，所以这个词常标记日常生活的边界。

senses.title: Not to be seriously considered
senses.definition: used in negative or emphatic statements to say that something is impossible or unacceptable
senses.definitionCN: 在否定或强调句中使用，表示某事不可能或不可接受
senses.example: Leaving the children alone overnight is unimaginable.
senses.exampleCN: 让孩子们独自过夜是无法想象的事。
senses.why: Social usage turns the word into a firm judgement: what one would never imagine becomes what one will not permit.
senses.whyCN: 社会用法把这个词变成坚定的判断：一个人绝不会去想象的事，就变成了绝不能允许的事。

intro.en: Unimaginable is built in English from the negative prefix un- and imaginable, which comes from the Latin verb imaginari, to picture in the mind.
intro.cn: unimaginable 在英语中由否定前缀 un- 与 imaginable 构成，后者源自在心中描绘的拉丁语动词 imaginari。

items.en: Imago means an image or likeness, and imaginari means to picture something in the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 意为形象、图像，imaginari 意为在心中描绘。

items.en: Medieval writers develop imaginatio for the faculty of forming images.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁作家用 imaginatio 表示形成形象的能力。

items.en: Imaginer carries the verb into French with the sense of picturing.
items.cn: 古法语 imaginer 承接这个动词，义为描绘、想象。

items.en: Imagination and imagine enter English through French, and imaginable follows as a formable adjective.
items.cn: imagination 与 imagine 经法语进入英语，imaginable 作为可构成的形容词随之出现。

items.en: Un- joins imaginable, and unimaginable begins to describe the vast, the shocking, and the impossible.
items.cn: un- 加到 imaginable 前，unimaginable 开始用来描述浩瀚、骇人与不可能之事。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to social judgements and to new technology.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到社会判断与新技术领域。

note.en: Unimaginable belongs to the image family built on Latin imago and is close to inconceivable and incredible.
note.cn: unimaginable 属于以拉丁语 imago 为根的 image 词族，在意思上接近 inconceivable 与 incredible。

entries.definition: able to be imagined
the ability to form pictures in the mind
in a way too great to picture
too strange or unlikely to be believed
entries.definitionCN: 无法想象的；不可思议的

entries.definition: difficult to believe
extremely surprising

normalIntro.en: Unimaginable is imaginable with the door of the mind shut, built on the Latin image that begins the whole word family.
normalIntro.cn: unimaginable 就是关上了想象之门的 imaginable，整族词都建在拉丁语表示「形象」的 imago 之上。

normal.en: The Latin root imago means an image, so imagine is to form a picture.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 imago 意为形象，所以 imagine 就是形成一幅图景。

normal.en: The suffix -able means able to be, and -ation builds imagination.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 表示「可以被」，-ation 构成 imagination。

normal.en: Un- negates imaginable, so the word says the picture cannot be drawn.
normal.cn: un- 否定 imaginable，说明这幅画根本画不出来。

normal.en: Almost unimaginable is a common hedge in academic writing.
normal.cn: almost unimaginable 是学术写作中常见的缓和说法。

normal.en: Compare inconceivable: it stresses thought, unimaginable stresses pictures in the mind.
normal.cn: 对比 inconceivable：前者强调思考，后者强调脑海中的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a painter staring at a canvas that stays blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家盯着始终空白的画布。

abstract.en: Imagine a box too wide for your arms to reach around.
abstract.cn: 想象一个宽得你双臂都抱不过来的箱子。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph whose centre is a pure white hole.
abstract.cn: 想想一张照片，正中间是一个纯白的大洞。

examples.en: The city suffered damage on an unimaginable scale.
examples.cn: 这座城市遭受了规模难以想象的破坏。

examples.en: To her grandparents, such a journey would have been unimaginable.
examples.cn: 对她的祖父母来说，这样的旅程是难以想象的。

examples.en: Modern surgery can save lives in ways that were unimaginable years ago.
examples.cn: 现代外科手术能以多年前难以想象的方式挽救生命。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺 imagine 不了」——连「俺」都想象不出来，自然就是难以想象的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语否定前缀 un-（不）+ 拉丁语 imago（形象）→ imaginari（描绘）→ imagine / imaginable（可想象的）→ unimaginable（难以想象的），核心义「想象力够不到」。

sensesIntro.en: Unimaginable starts from scale beyond the mind, moves to disbelief and suffering, then to what has never been thought of, beyond experience, and finally to what must not be allowed.
sensesIntro.cn: unimaginable 从超出头脑的规模出发，过渡到难以置信与苦难，再到从未被想到的事物、超出经验之事，最后落到绝不允许发生的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a canvas that stays blank where the picture should be.
core.cn: 核心意象：脑海中画到一半就空白了的画布。

branches.en: Scale and size too great for the mind is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 规模大到头脑无法容纳，是首要义项。

branches.en: Disbelief follows when the picture cannot be built at all.
branches.cn: 画面完全画不出来时，紧随其后的就是难以置信。

branches.en: Suffering nobody can picture gives the emotional sense.
branches.cn: 无人能想象的苦难构成其情感义项。

branches.en: What has never been thought of and what lies beyond experience both sit past the edge of imagination.
branches.cn: 从未被想到的事物与超出经验之事，都站在想象的边缘之外。

branches.en: A judgement of disbelief can harden into a ruling that something is impossible.
branches.cn: 难以置信的判断可以硬化成「此事不可能」的定论。

intro.en: Unimaginable joins the negative un-, the Latin root imago, and the suffix -able, with imagine, imagination, and imaginative nearby.
intro.cn: unimaginable 由否定前缀 un-、拉丁词根 imago 与后缀 -able 合成，旁边还有 imagine、imagination 与 imaginative。

latinIntro.en: Latin imago means an image, and imaginari means to picture something in the mind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imago 意为形象，imaginari 意为在心中描绘。

items.example: The prefix un- negates imaginable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定 imaginable。

items.example: Imago gives the family its image core.
items.exampleCN: imago 给这个词族提供了「形象」的核心。

items.example: Imaginari is the ancestor of imagine.
items.exampleCN: imaginari 是 imagine 的祖先。

items.meaning: to form a picture in the mind
items.example: Imagine is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: imagine 是基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms imaginable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 imaginable。

items.example: Imaginable is the base adjective.
items.exampleCN: imaginable 是基础形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms imagination.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 imagination。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms imaginative.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 imaginative。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unimaginably.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 unimaginably。

definition_zh: 缺乏了解的；无知的；不掌握情况或信息的；未受过教育的
definition_en: not having enough knowledge or information about something, or not having been given the facts
core_image: 一扇关着的档案柜门：里面有机密文件，外面的人却一无所知
scene: 出发前有人随口问了句那边的新政策，才发现没人真正了解。The official admitted that he had been uninformed about the changes.
sceneCN: 这里 uninformed 是「不掌握情况的」（第 3 个义项：没有获知事实或内情）；句意为这位官员承认自己对那些变动毫不知情。

pos.zh: 形容词：缺乏了解的；无知的；不掌握信息的；未受教育的

collocations.zh: 在信息不足的情况下作出的决定

derivatives.zh: 由 in- + form 构成的基础词，义为「了解情况的；有知识的」
动词 inform 加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「告知；提供信息」
inform + -ative，义为「提供有用信息的」
uninformed + -ness，义为「无知的状态」
mis- + informed，义为「被误导的；得到错误信息的」

senses.title: Not educated or not having access to knowledge
senses.definition: having received little education or having no access to reliable knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 受教育不多，或接触不到可靠知识的
senses.example: The plan was meant for both experts and uninformed readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这套方案既面向专家，也面向没有专业知识的读者。
senses.why: The core is a mind that has not been shaped by knowledge, so the first sense names the general lack of learning.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个没有被知识塑造过的头脑，所以第一个义项指普遍的「缺乏学问」。

senses.title: Based on no knowledge
senses.definition: formed or made without proper knowledge or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在缺乏适当知识或证据的情况下形成或作出的
senses.example: An uninformed guess is often worse than an honest question.
senses.exampleCN: 没有依据的猜测往往还不如一个诚实的提问。
senses.why: When the gap is in the act itself, a decision, a guess or an opinion becomes groundless.
senses.whyCN: 当这种「知识缺口」落在行为本身时，决定、猜测或看法就变得没有根据。

senses.title: Not given the facts
senses.titleCN: 不掌握情况的；不知情的
senses.definition: not having been told the necessary facts or information
senses.definitionCN: 没有被告知必要事实或信息的
senses.example: Some workers were uninformed about the new safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 有些工人对新的安全规定并不知情。
senses.why: Here the missing knowledge is about a current situation, and the usual cause is that nobody passed the facts on.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺的是关于当下情况的信息，而常见原因是没有人把事实传达出去。

senses.title: Lacking knowledge of a particular subject
senses.definition: without special knowledge of a specific subject or field
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏某一特定主题或领域的专门知识
senses.example: I am uninformed on matters of international law.
senses.exampleCN: 我对国际法方面的事务缺乏了解。
senses.why: A specific field is simply the general lack of knowledge limited to one domain, often used politely about oneself.
senses.whyCN: 特定领域只是把普遍的「缺乏知识」限定在一个领域，还常用来自谦。

senses.title: Not advised by experts
senses.definition: carried out without expert advice or due consultation
senses.definitionCN: 在没有专家意见或充分咨询的情况下进行的
senses.example: The town took an uninformed risk when it ignored its engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小镇忽视了工程师的意见，冒了一次不明底细的风险。
senses.why: The gap may be filled by experts, so a choice made without consulting them is called uninformed.
senses.whyCN: 这种知识缺口本可以由专家来填补，所以没有咨询专家就作的选择被称作 uninformed。

intro.en: Uninformed is the negative of informed, from Latin informare, to shape or give form to the mind.
intro.cn: uninformed 是 informed 的否定形式，源自拉丁语 informare（塑造、赋予形状）。

items.en: Informare literally means to shape or give form, and later to instruct the mind.
items.cn: informare 字面义为「塑形、赋予形状」，后来引申为「教导、使心智成形」。

items.en: Forma, the noun behind it, means shape, figure or model.
items.cn: 它背后的名词 forma 意为形状、形体或模子。

items.en: Enformer carries the sense of instructing or teaching into French.
items.cn: 古法语 enformer 把「教导、告知」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Inform enters English with the sense of instructing or giving knowledge.
items.cn: inform 进入英语时，意为教导、传授知识。

items.en: Informed first names the shaped mind and later the possession of information, so uninformed means the mind has not been shaped.
items.cn: informed 先指被塑造过的心智，后来指掌握信息，因此 uninformed 表示心智尚未被塑造，缺乏知识。

note.en: Uninformed is the negative of informed, close to unaware and ignorant, and it contrasts with informed and knowledgeable.
note.cn: uninformed 是 informed 的否定形式，与 unaware、ignorant 相近，并与 informed、knowledgeable 相对。

entries.definition: having knowledge or being told the facts
to tell someone the facts
involving a single variable; only the first syllable is shared, and this word has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 涉及单一变量的；只是开头拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not knowing that something exists or is happening
entries.definitionCN: 没有意识到的；不知道的

entries.definition: lacking knowledge or information, often used unfavourably
entries.definitionCN: 无知的；不了解的（常带贬义）

entries.definition: having had little or no formal schooling
entries.definitionCN: 未受过正规教育的；没有文化的

normalIntro.en: Break uninformed into un- plus informed: the mind has not yet been informed.
normalIntro.cn: 把 uninformed 拆成 un- 与 informed：心智还没有被「告知」。

normal.en: The negative prefix un- can be attached directly to informed.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 un- 可以直接加在 informed 前面。

normal.en: The base verb inform means to tell someone the facts.
normal.cn: 基础动词 inform 意为告知某人事实。

normal.en: Informed decisions are based on full information, so uninformed decisions are not.
normal.cn: informed decision 有充分信息作依据，uninformed decision 则没有。

normal.en: Be informed about a plan, never be uninformed about it.
normal.cn: 要用 be informed about 了解一个计划，别对它一无所知。

normal.en: Compare unaware: unaware is a passing state, uninformed is a lasting lack of knowledge.
normal.cn: 对比 unaware：unaware 是暂时的状态，uninformed 是长期的缺乏知识。

abstract.en: Picture a mind printed from a blank sheet with nothing written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张白纸印出的心智，上面一个字也没有。

abstract.en: Imagine an arrow shot in fog with no landmark in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中射出一支箭，四周没有任何地标。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed envelope that no messenger ever delivered.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的信封，送信人始终没有送到。

examples.en: The debate turned noisy because many speakers were uninformed about the facts.
examples.cn: 讨论变得吵闹，因为许多发言人并不了解事实。

examples.en: An uninformed choice can cost a company a lot of money.
examples.cn: 不明底细的选择可能让公司损失很多钱。

examples.en: The guide avoided technical terms for uninformed visitors.
examples.cn: 向导避免使用术语，以便照顾没有专业背景的游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安-因弗姆德」——原来「因弗」这个闭目坐着的人一直「没被通知」，什么都不知道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 un-（不）+ informed（已获知识的）→ uninformed；informed 源自拉丁语 informare（塑造、使成形）→ 古法语 enformer（教导）→ 中古英语 inform（告知）。核心义「心智未被塑造」。

sensesIntro.en: Uninformed first names a mind without knowledge, then a groundless act, a person not told the facts, one field one does not know, and finally a choice made without expert advice.
sensesIntro.cn: uninformed 先指没有知识的头脑，再指没有根据的行为、没有被告知事实的人、不熟悉的某个领域，最后指未经专家咨询的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed archive cabinet, with the person outside knowing nothing inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：关着的档案柜，门外的人对柜内一无所知。

branches.en: THE MIND: a mind never shaped by learning stays without knowledge.
branches.cn: 心智线：从未被知识塑造的头脑始终缺乏学问。

branches.en: THE ACT: a guess or decision without knowledge is groundless.
branches.cn: 行为线：没有知识支撑的猜测或决定便没有根据。

branches.en: THE NEWS: a person cut off from the facts is not told what is happening.
branches.cn: 消息线：被隔绝于事实之外的人没有被告知发生了什么。

branches.en: THE FIELD: one particular subject may lie outside a person knowledge.
branches.cn: 领域线：某一个特定学科可能落在某人知识范围之外。

branches.en: All three senses describe a gap that teaching, telling or expert advice could fill.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都描述一个可由教导、告知或专家建议来填补的缺口。

intro.en: Uninformed is built from the negative prefix un-, the Latin verb form- meaning to shape, and the past participle ending -ed.
intro.cn: uninformed 由否定前缀 un-、拉丁语动词词根 form-（塑造）与过去分词词尾 -ed 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma means shape or form, and informare means to shape or give form to, later to instruct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 forma 意为形状或形式，informare 意为塑形、赋予形状，后来指教导。

items.example: The prefix un- marks the absence of knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 表示缺乏知识。

items.example: The Latin prefix in- carries the sense of putting form into material.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 表示把形状放入材料之中。

items.example: The root form- gives the idea of shaping a mind.
items.exampleCN: 词根 form- 给出「塑造心智」的意象。

items.example: The verb informare links shaping matter with teaching.
items.exampleCN: 动词 informare 把塑形与教导联系起来。

items.example: Inform still carries the teaching sense.
items.exampleCN: inform 仍保留教导的意味。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms informing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 informing。

items.meaningCN: 表示已然的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms informed, the shaped mind.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 informed，即被塑造过的心智。

items.example: Informed is the base of uninformed.
items.exampleCN: informed 是 uninformed 的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ative forms informative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ative 构成 informative。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms uninformedness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 uninformedness。

definition_zh: 无人居住的；荒无人烟的；无人烟居住的（指房屋或土地）
definition_en: with no people living there, or with nobody occupying a place such as a house or a room
core_image: 一座空房子：门窗紧闭，屋里没有灯，也没有人的脚步声
scene: 地图上那串小岛被标成空白，过去几十年里连捕鱼船都很少靠近。The island was left uninhabited after the last fishing fleet moved away.
sceneCN: 这里 uninhabited 是「无人居住的」（第 1 个义项：没有人住在那里）；句意为最后一支捕鱼船队离开后，这座岛就无人居住了。

pos.zh: 形容词：无人居住的；荒无人烟的

derivatives.zh: in- + habit 构成的基础动词，义为「居住于；栖居于」
inhabit + -ant，义为「居民；栖居动物」
inhabit + -able，义为「可居住的」
un- + inhabitable，义为「不适宜居住的」
habit + -ation，义为「居住；住所」

senses.title: Having no people living there
senses.definition: having no people living in or on it
senses.definitionCN: 其中没有人在那里居住的
senses.example: The remote island has been uninhabited for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座偏远的岛屿已经五十年无人居住。
senses.why: The core image is a place with nobody living in it, so this sense follows directly from the habit root.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是没人住在里面的地方，所以这个义项直接来自 habit（居住）这一词根。

senses.title: Empty of people at the moment
senses.titleCN: 空置的；（房屋）无人使用的
senses.definition: not occupied by anyone at a particular time, like a house or a room left empty
senses.definitionCN: 在特定时间没有被人占用，如空置的房屋或房间
senses.example: The house stood uninhabited while the family lived abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人住在国外期间，房子一直空置。
senses.why: A house that nobody occupies is uninhabited, even if people could move in tomorrow.
senses.whyCN: 没人占用的房屋就是 uninhabited，哪怕明天就可能有人搬进来。

senses.title: Without human settlement
senses.definition: having no human settlement or development
senses.definitionCN: 没有人类聚落或开发的
senses.example: Much of the desert is uninhabited and almost impassable.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沙漠大部分无人烟，几乎无法通行。
senses.why: When the lack of people extends across a whole region, the word describes empty wilderness.
senses.whyCN: 当「无人」扩展到整个区域时，这个词就描述空旷的荒野。

senses.title: Not occupied by creatures
senses.definition: not occupied by people or animals at all
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有人类或动物栖息的
senses.example: The cave was uninhabited, with no tracks on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 那个洞穴没有任何生物栖息，地上连一个脚印都没有。
senses.why: In zoology, a burrow, a nest or a hive may also be untouched, so the word can name any empty home.
senses.whyCN: 在动物学中，洞穴、巢或蜂箱也可能无人无兽，因此这个词也能指任何一种空着住不进去的家。

senses.title: Permanently deserted
senses.definition: left permanently empty because residents have all moved away
senses.definitionCN: 因为居民全部迁走而永久空置的
senses.example: The old mining village was left uninhabited after the pit closed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场关闭后，这座旧矿村便荒废无人。
senses.why: When the emptiness becomes permanent, a settlement passes into the state of abandonment.
senses.whyCN: 当空置变成永久时，聚落就进入了被废弃的状态。

intro.en: Uninhabited is the negative of inhabited, built from Latin habitare, to dwell or live in.
intro.cn: uninhabited 是 inhabited 的否定形式，来自拉丁语 habitare（居住、栖居）。

items.en: Habitare means to dwell or to live in a place.
items.cn: habitare 意为居住、栖居在某地。

items.en: The link between habitare and the verb habere, to have, is uncertain; the idea is generally taken to be having a place as one dwells in it.
items.cn: habitare 与 habere（拥有）之间的联系来源不确定；一般认为，「拥有」的含义引申为「拥有一个安居之所」。

items.en: Inhabitare adds the prefix in- and means to dwell in.
items.cn: inhabitare 加上前缀 in-，意为住在……之中。

items.en: Inhabitare is continued in English through French influence.
items.cn: inhabitare 经由法语影响继续传入英语。

items.en: Inhabited is formed from the past participle, and uninhabited is its negative.
items.cn: inhabited 由过去分词构成，uninhabited 则是它的否定形式。

note.en: Uninhabited is close to deserted and empty, and it contrasts with inhabited, populated and occupied.
note.cn: uninhabited 与 deserted、empty 相近，并与 inhabited、populated、occupied 相对。

entries.definition: having people living there
to live in a place
free to act without restraint; only the spelling is close, and this word has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 不拘束的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: empty of people because they have all left
not occupied by anyone at the moment
not being used or lived in by anyone

normalIntro.en: Break uninhabited into un- plus inhabited: nobody inhabits the place any more.
normalIntro.cn: 把 uninhabited 拆成 un- 与 inhabited：已经没有人居住在那个地方。

normal.en: The negative prefix un- turns inhabited into uninhabited.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 un- 把 inhabited 变成 uninhabited。

normal.en: The base verb inhabit means to live in a place.
normal.cn: 基础动词 inhabit 意为居住在某地。

normal.en: An inhabitant is a person or animal that lives there.
normal.cn: inhabitant 就是住在那里的居民或动物。

normal.en: An uninhabited island needs enough fresh water to be a home.
normal.cn: 要成为家，无人岛需要充足的淡水。

normal.en: Compare unoccupied: unoccupied fits rooms, uninhabited fits islands and buildings.
normal.cn: 对比 unoccupied：unoccupied 用于房间，uninhabited 用于岛屿和房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with dust and no footprints on the step.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门口积着灰，台阶上没有脚印。

abstract.en: Imagine a fishing village where all the boats have gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个渔村，所有的船都开走了。

abstract.en: Think of a bird nest still kept for a while after the birds have flown.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟巢在鸟儿飞走之后还空挂了好一阵。

examples.en: The remote island is uninhabited but rich in wildlife.
examples.cn: 这座偏远的岛无人居住，但野生动植物丰富。

examples.en: The house had been uninhabited since the owner moved abroad.
examples.cn: 自从房主移居国外，这栋房子就一直空着。

examples.en: Winters in this region are severe and the heath is uninhabited.
examples.cn: 这个地区的冬天极为寒冷，荒原上人迹罕至。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安-因哈比特-德」——「因」为没有「含比」的居民在这里「比特」，所以岛屿空空无人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 un-（不）+ inhabited（有人居住的）→ uninhabited；inhabited 源自拉丁语 inhabitare（住在……中）= in-（在内）+ habitare（居住），habitare 与 habere（拥有）的联系一般认为来自「拥有住所」的引申，确切关系来源不确定。核心义「没有人住在里面」。

sensesIntro.en: Uninhabited first describes a place with no residents, then an empty house or room, then a region without settlement, then a home without creatures, and finally a village left forever.
sensesIntro.cn: uninhabited 先描述无人居住的地方，再指空置的房屋或房间、没有聚落的地区、没有任何生物栖息的居所，最后指被永久废弃的村落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty house with closed windows and no lamp inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座窗门紧闭、屋里没有灯的空房子。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a land with no residents is the defining sense.
branches.cn: 地方线：没有居民的土地是核心义项。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: an unoccupied home is uninhabited even if people may return.
branches.cn: 房屋线：无人占用的家就是 uninhabited，即便人可能回来。

branches.en: THE REGION: a whole territory without settlement is wild land.
branches.cn: 区域线：没有聚落的整片区域就是荒野。

branches.en: THE HOME OF CREATURES: a nest or burrow can be empty too.
branches.cn: 巢穴线：动物的巢或穴同样可能是空的。

branches.en: When residents never come back, an uninhabited place turns into a deserted one.
branches.cn: 当居民再也不回来时，无人居住之地就变成了被废弃之地。

intro.en: Uninhabited stacks the negative prefix un-, the Latin prefix in-, and the root habit- meaning to dwell.
intro.cn: uninhabited 叠加了否定前缀 un-、拉丁语前缀 in- 与词根 habit-（居住）。

latinIntro.en: Latin habitare means to dwell, and inhabitare means to dwell in a place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habitare 意为居住，inhabitare 意为住在某地。

items.example: The prefix un- marks the absence of residents.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 表示没有居民。

items.example: The Latin prefix in- means dwelling inside a place.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 in- 表示住在某地之内。

items.example: The root habit- carries the idea of a home.
items.exampleCN: 词根 habit- 承载「家」的意象。

items.example: Habitare is the dwelling verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: habitare 是这一词族的「居住」动词。

items.example: Inhabit keeps the dwelling sense.
items.exampleCN: inhabit 保留居住含义。

items.example: The suffix -ant names a person who dwells.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 指居住的人。

items.example: The suffix -able forms inhabitable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 inhabitable。

items.meaningCN: 表示已然的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms inhabited.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 inhabited。

items.example: Inhabited is the base of uninhabited.
items.exampleCN: inhabited 是 uninhabited 的基础。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms habitation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 habitation。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from in- plus habitare

definition_zh: 不引人注目的；不打扰人的；谦逊低调的；（风格）含蓄的
definition_en: not attracting attention or not annoying other people, often deliberately quiet or modest
core_image: 墙角的一盏小灯：光线正好照亮书页，却不会刺眼，也不会抢走目光
scene: 会议室的角落里，工作人员轻声提醒客人，尽量不惊动正在发言的人。The assistant waited in an unobtrusive corner until the speech was over.
sceneCN: 这里 unobtrusive 是「不引人注目的」（第 1 个义项：不吸引别人注意）；句意为助理在不起眼的角落里等候，直到演讲结束。

pos.zh: 形容词：不引人注目的；不打扰人的；谦逊的；含蓄的

derivatives.zh: un- + obtrusive，基础形容词，义为「突出的；惹眼的；唐突的」
unobtrusive + -ness，义为「不引人注目；低调」
unobtrusive + -ly，义为「不惹眼地；不打扰地」
同源动词，义为「强行提出；闯入；冒出来」

senses.title: Not attracting attention
senses.definition: not drawing other people notice in an obvious way
senses.definitionCN: 不引人注意、不以显眼的方式吸引人目光的
senses.example: She chose a quiet, unobtrusive colour for the curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 她给窗帘选了安静而不惹眼的颜色。
senses.why: The core is a thing that does not push itself into view, so this sense names the simple absence of attention.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是不把自身推到别人眼前的东西，所以这个义项就是「不吸引注意」本身。

senses.title: Not causing disturbance
senses.definition: not disturbing or annoying other people
senses.definitionCN: 不干扰或打扰他人的
senses.example: The nurse moved around the ward in an unobtrusive way.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在病房里走动，不惊扰病人。
senses.why: Besides being seen, a person can be heard or felt, and an unobtrusive act stays out of the way.
senses.whyCN: 除了被看见，一个人还可能被听见或被注意到，而不张扬的行为则会避开这些干扰。

senses.title: Deliberately modest
senses.definition: deliberately modest, without seeking credit or praise
senses.definitionCN: 有意保持低调、不追求赞誉的
senses.example: He handled the crisis in a calm and unobtrusive way.
senses.exampleCN: 他以冷静而低调的方式处理了这场危机。
senses.why: The restraint may be a conscious choice, and the word then praises someone quiet and self-effacing.
senses.whyCN: 这种克制可能是有意为之，于是这个词便用来称赞一个安静而谦逊的人。

senses.title: Hidden but useful
senses.definition: placed out of notice yet still doing its job well
senses.definitionCN: 不显眼地安置，却仍能发挥作用
senses.example: The lighting was unobtrusive but bright enough to read by.
senses.exampleCN: 灯光不显眼，却足够亮，能看书。
senses.why: Things can work quietly in the background, serving people without being seen as interference.
senses.whyCN: 东西可以在背景里安静地工作，为人服务却不被视为干扰。

senses.title: Understated in style
senses.definition: quiet and restrained in style or design
senses.definitionCN: 风格或设计上安静、有分寸的
senses.example: The book has an unobtrusive cover that ages well.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的封面毫不张扬，经得起时间。
senses.why: Understated design is simply the visible form of not wanting to stand out.
senses.whyCN: 不张扬的设计，只是「不想出头」在外观上的表现。

intro.en: Unobtrusive is un- plus obtrusive, from Latin obtrudere, to thrust or push against someone.
intro.cn: unobtrusive 是 un- 加 obtrusive，来自拉丁语 obtrudere（推挤、强行塞给）。

items.en: Obtrudere means to push or thrust against, or to force on someone.
items.cn: obtrudere 意为推挤、硬塞给别人。

items.en: The verb joins ob-, meaning against or towards, with trudere, to push.
items.cn: 这个动词由表示「对着、朝向」的 ob- 与「推」的 trudere 组成。

items.en: Obtrusus and obtrusio give the family a second life in Latin prose as pushing oneself forward.
items.cn: obtrusus 与 obtrusio 让这一词族在拉丁语散文中重新活跃，指强行出头。

items.en: English forms obtrude, obtrusion and the adjective obtrusive.
items.cn: 英语据此构出 obtrude、obtrusion 及形容词 obtrusive。

items.en: The negative unobtrusive becomes common, praising people who stay out of the way.
items.cn: 否定形式 unobtrusive 逐渐通行，用于称赞不抢风头的人。

note.en: Unobtrusive is close to discreet and inconspicuous, and it contrasts with obtrusive and intrusive.
note.cn: unobtrusive 与 discreet、inconspicuous 相近，并与 obtrusive、intrusive 相对。

entries.definition: noticeable in a way that annoys people
to push oneself forward
coming in where one is not wanted; it shares the Latin root trudere with obtrusive
entries.definitionCN: 侵入的；打搅的；与 obtrusive 共享拉丁词根 trudere

entries.definition: not easily noticed
careful not to attract attention
modest and not claiming importance

normalIntro.en: Break unobtrusive into un- plus obtrusive: nothing is pushed towards the viewer or the listener.
normalIntro.cn: 把 unobtrusive 拆成 un- 与 obtrusive：没有东西被硬推到看者和听者面前。

normal.en: The negative prefix un- turns obtrusive into unobtrusive.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 un- 把 obtrusive 变成 unobtrusive。

normal.en: The Latin root trudere means to push, so obtrusive means pushing into view.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 trudere 意为推，所以 obtrusive 就是「推到眼前」。

normal.en: Compare obtrude, which means to force oneself or an opinion on others.
normal.cn: 对比 obtrude，意为把自己或某个观点强加于人。

normal.en: Unobtrusive fits manners, design, lighting and staff, wherever quiet help is wanted.
normal.cn: unobtrusive 适合形容举止、设计、灯光与员工，凡需要安静地起作用之处皆可用。

normal.en: Compare quiet: quiet is about sound, unobtrusive is about being noticed at all.
normal.cn: 对比 quiet：quiet 说的是声音，unobtrusive 说的是是否被注意到。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lights the page without catching your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮书页，却不夺人目光。

abstract.en: Imagine a waiter who fills your glass without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一位侍者悄无声息地给你续水。

abstract.en: Think of a coat that matches the grey wall behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套正好与身后的灰墙融为一体。

examples.en: The hotel staff were friendly but unobtrusive.
examples.cn: 酒店员工友好，却不打扰客人。

examples.en: The new signs are unobtrusive and fit the old town well.
examples.cn: 新设的标牌很不显眼，与古镇颇为相称。

examples.en: She kept an unobtrusive watch on the children from the corner.
examples.cn: 她在角落里不引人注意地照看着孩子们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「按-欧不-楚西弗」——欧不把自己推出来，所以毫不惹眼；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 un-（不）+ obtrusive（惹眼的、唐突的）→ unobtrusive；obtrusive 源自拉丁语 obtrudere = ob-（对着、朝向）+ trudere（推），字面义「推到面前」。核心义「不把自己推到别人面前」。

sensesIntro.en: Unobtrusive begins with what escapes notice, then what avoids disturbing people, then a deliberate modesty, a hidden practicality, and finally an understated style.
sensesIntro.cn: unobtrusive 先说躲开注视的东西，再说避免打扰别人的行为，然后是刻意的谦逊、隐蔽的实用，最后是不张扬的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small lamp in a corner that lights the page without catching the eye.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙角的小灯照亮书页，却不夺人目光。

branches.en: BECOMING SEEN: a thing that does not push itself into view is overlooked.
branches.cn: 被看见线：不把自己推到眼前的事物便不会被注意到。

branches.en: STAYING QUIET: unobtrusive behaviour avoids noise and fuss.
branches.cn: 安静线：不张扬的举止避开噪音与慌乱。

branches.en: STEPPING BACK: modesty is a choice to keep out of the spotlight.
branches.cn: 退后线：谦逊是有意不站在聚光灯下。

branches.en: HELPING QUIETLY: useful things work in the background.
branches.cn: 默默服务线：有用的东西在背景中工作。

branches.en: Understated style is the look of something that does not want to be noticed.
branches.cn: 不张扬的风格，就是「不想被注意」的外观。

intro.en: Unobtrusive is built from the negative prefix un-, the Latin prefix ob-, the root trud- meaning to push, and the suffix -ive.
intro.cn: unobtrusive 由否定前缀 un-、拉丁语前缀 ob-、词根 trud-（推）与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin trudere means to push, and obtrudere means to push against or force on someone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trudere 意为推，obtrudere 意为推撞、强加于人。

items.example: The prefix un- removes the unwanted attention.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 去掉那种不受欢迎的注意。

items.example: The Latin prefix ob- points the push towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语前缀 ob- 把「推」的方向指向别人。

items.example: The root trud- gives the pushing image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 trud- 提供推挤的意象。

items.meaning: to push against, to force on
items.example: Obtrudere is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: obtrudere 是这一词族的直接来源。

items.example: Obtrude keeps the sense of pushing in.
items.exampleCN: obtrude 保留「强行挤入」的意味。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或倾向的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ive forms obtrusive and unobtrusive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 obtrusive 与 unobtrusive。

items.example: Obtrusive is the base of unobtrusive.
items.exampleCN: obtrusive 是 unobtrusive 的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms unobtrusiveness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 unobtrusiveness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unobtrusively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 unobtrusively。

items.example: Trudere gives the whole pushing family.
items.exampleCN: trudere 提供整个「推」词族。
